introduction.en: Which descriptions feel relatively closer to your past month? This original FermatMind Web repair keeps twenty-five owned Mini themes, with new questions and transparent counts. It is not the original thirty-one-question bank or another site’s twenty-seven-type edition.
introduction.zh: 过去一个月，哪些描述相对更像自己？费马Web修订版沿用二十五个自有小程序主题，新写题目并明示次数。它不是三十一题原题本，也不是其他网站的二十七型版本。

instructions.zh: 回看最近一个月的日常时刻，选两种描述中更像自己的一种，而不是选哪种更好。如果都不适合，可以退出，不必勉强作答。
instructions.en: Think about ordinary moments in the past month. Choose which description fits your recent responses better, rather than which sounds better. You can leave without a result if neither fits.

summary.en: In this edition, Self-Critic names a set of choices about the tone of self-review: noticing what remains unfinished, anticipating criticism, or returning to a perceived mistake after a task is over. A higher count means you selected these particular descriptions more often against their four scheduled alternatives. It does not establish how often you criticize yourself in everyday life.
summary.zh: 本版“自我苛责者”指向一组关于自我复盘口气的选择：先看到没做好的地方、预想批评，或事情结束后仍回看一个失误。次数较高，只说明你在安排好的四组比较里较常选择这些描述，不能据此算出日常苛责自己的频率。

title.en: Self-Critic | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 自我苛责者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Self-Critic theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“自我苛责者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: What this label records
title.zh: 这个标签记录什么

paragraphs.en: In this edition, Self-Critic names a set of choices about the tone of self-review: noticing what remains unfinished, anticipating criticism, or returning to a perceived mistake after a task is over. A higher count means you selected these particular descriptions more often against their four scheduled alternatives. It does not establish how often you criticize yourself in everyday life.
paragraphs.zh: 本版“自我苛责者”指向一组关于自我复盘口气的选择：先看到没做好的地方、预想批评，或事情结束后仍回看一个失误。次数较高，只说明你在安排好的四组比较里较常选择这些描述，不能据此算出日常苛责自己的频率。

paragraphs.en: The useful question is whether a description resembles a recent moment you recognize. You might agree with one example and reject another. That difference is worth keeping. You do not have to accept the nickname as an identity, and a lower count is not evidence that you lack standards or care less about your work.
paragraphs.zh: 更有用的问题是：某条描述是否像最近一个自己认得的时刻。你可能认同一个例子，却不认同另一个，这种差别值得保留。你不必把昵称认作身份；次数较低，也不说明你没有标准或不在乎自己的事情。

title.en: A small mistake becomes a larger verdict
title.zh: 小失误怎样变成大判决

paragraphs.en: Imagine sending a draft and later noticing one unclear sentence. There is a concrete job available: clarify the sentence or ask whether it caused confusion. Self-critical review can add a second job that was never requested, such as rehearsing what the sentence supposedly proves about your overall competence or how the reader must now see you.
paragraphs.zh: 比如发出一份初稿后，发现一句话不够清楚。眼前有个具体任务：补清那句话，或确认它是否造成误解。苛刻复盘却可能额外加上一项没人要求的工作：反复想这句话证明自己整体有多差，或收件人现在一定怎样看自己。

paragraphs.en: Those are different questions. A reader asking for a clearer example has not necessarily made a judgment about you as a person. Equally, a real error does not disappear because the quiz calls your response a theme. Look at the actual comment, consequence and correction needed before treating the whole situation as a personal verdict.
paragraphs.zh: 这是两种不同的问题。读者希望例子更清楚，不一定是在评价你这个人；另一方面，游戏把反应叫作一个主题，也不会让真实错误消失。先看实际反馈、后果和需要补的动作，再决定是否有必要给整件事下一个关于自己的总判决。

title.en: Standards need a stopping point
title.zh: 标准也需要停止条件

paragraphs.en: Careful review has a practical use when it identifies something specific that can be checked. You might notice a missing assumption, an ambiguous promise or a step that needs another pair of eyes. The nickname does not prove this skill, but a particular example may show you where reviewing was useful.
paragraphs.zh: 复盘能指出一件可核对的具体事情时，就有实际用途：比如漏掉一个条件、承诺不够明确，或某一步需要再请人看一眼。昵称不能证明你具有这种能力，但具体例子可以帮助你看出哪一次检查确实有用。

paragraphs.en: The cost can appear when the standard keeps moving after the relevant check is complete. Another reread may offer no new information while delaying the next task. Distinguish a correction that changes the work from a repeated accusation that only changes the mood in which you are doing it. The result cannot make that distinction for you.
paragraphs.zh: 代价可能出现在检查已经做完、标准却仍不断后退的时候。又读一遍未必带来新信息，却会推迟下一件事。可以区分真正改变作品的修改，和只改变做事心情的重复责备；这份结果不能代你完成这个区分。

title.en: Self-Critic, Thinker and Low-Battery Rebuilder
title.zh: 与思考者、低电量整备者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Reflective Thinker concerns examining an explanation or understanding how a problem fits together. Self-Critic concerns the evaluation directed at yourself while doing so. Someone can examine a problem in detail without being harsh, or be harsh while barely examining the problem. Similar counts do not turn these into one hidden psychological scale.
paragraphs.zh: “反复思考者”关注怎样检查解释、理解问题的结构；“自我苛责者”关注做这件事时如何评价自己。一个人可以想得细而不苛刻，也可能责备很多却没真正分析问题。次数相近，不会使它们自动成为同一条隐藏心理量表。

paragraphs.en: Low-Battery Rebuilder concerns making room for a manageable next step when energy feels limited. A tired day and a severe inner commentary may coincide, but neither establishes the cause of the other. These are overlapping editorial examples, not mutually exclusive diagnoses, and a tie is allowed without choosing a more dramatic label.
paragraphs.zh: “低电量整备者”关注精力有限时怎样为一个做得到的小步骤留位置。疲惫和苛刻的自我评价可能碰巧同时出现，但都不能证明另一方的原因。这些编辑性例子可以重叠，不是互斥诊断；出现并列时，也无需挑一个更戏剧化的名字。

title.en: Try one bounded review
title.zh: 试一次有边界的复盘

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary, low-stakes task, write down the issue, one check and a stopping condition. An example is: “The instruction may be unclear; ask one reader to describe the next step; revise if that step differs from what I intended.” The point is to inspect an actual task, not to use a quiz result as a reason to become a different person.
paragraphs.zh: 可以选一件普通、低风险的小事，记下问题、一次核对和停止条件。比如：“说明可能不清楚；请一位读者说出下一步；如果与我的本意不同，再改。”目的是看清一项实际任务，而不是因为游戏结果就要求自己变成另一种人。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, notice whether another round would supply new information. If circumstances change, a new review may be appropriate. If nothing changes except the wording of the accusation, you can leave that accusation out of the task list. This is an optional reflection, not a treatment or a promise that one exercise will change distress.
paragraphs.zh: 事后可以看看：再来一轮能否获得新信息？情况变了，重新检查可能合理；如果变化的只是责备自己的说法，可以不把那句责备继续列进任务清单。这只是可选的日常观察，不是治疗，也不保证一次练习会改变困扰。

title.en: Keep the score and the person separate
title.zh: 把次数与人的价值分开

paragraphs.en: The fifty-choice Web repair uses four appearances of this theme, with two A and two B positions. Opponents differ between themes; the count is not a full ordering of twenty-five personality traits. It measures neither self-esteem nor mental health. The historical source code IMSB is retained for provenance, while insulting claims about a person’s worth are not adopted.
paragraphs.zh: 网页修订版共五十题，本主题出现四次，A、B各两次。不同主题遇到的比较对象不同，次数不是对二十五种人格特质的完整排序，也不测自尊或心理健康。旧主题码IMSB仅用于溯源，本版不采用给人的价值贴侮辱性标签的说法。

paragraphs.en: This public guide is the same for everyone and contains no personal count. You may return to the entry, compare another explanation or finish here. Private responses remain in page memory under the stated Web controls; copying the public entry does not copy an answer sheet. There is no requirement to share, sign up or take another assessment to read the full explanation.
paragraphs.zh: 这份公开指南对所有人相同，不含个人次数。你可以返回入口、比较其他解释，也可以读完就结束。私人回答按网页已说明的控制只留在页面内存；复制公开入口不会复制答卷。阅读完整解释不要求分享、注册，或再做另一项测评。

title.en: Initiator: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 带队推进者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Initiator collects choices about proposing a starting plan, suggesting priorities and following up an agreed action. These examples concern what you might choose to do when a shared task is unsettled. They do not establish that other people want you to lead, that your plan is correct or that you are good at managing a team.
summary.zh: “带队推进者”汇集了提出起步方案、建议先后顺序、跟进已约定动作的选择。这些例子关注共同任务尚未落定时，你可能选择做什么；不能证明别人希望由你领导、你的方案正确，或你擅长管理团队。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Initiator | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 带队推进者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Initiator theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“带队推进者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: An offered next step, not a leadership credential
title.zh: 提出下一步，不是领导资格

paragraphs.en: Initiator collects choices about proposing a starting plan, suggesting priorities and following up an agreed action. These examples concern what you might choose to do when a shared task is unsettled. They do not establish that other people want you to lead, that your plan is correct or that you are good at managing a team.
paragraphs.zh: “带队推进者”汇集了提出起步方案、建议先后顺序、跟进已约定动作的选择。这些例子关注共同任务尚未落定时，你可能选择做什么；不能证明别人希望由你领导、你的方案正确，或你擅长管理团队。

paragraphs.en: If this theme was selected often, start with one recent situation rather than a general conclusion about your personality. What was missing: a decision, a volunteer, information or agreement? Offering structure can answer one of those needs and miss another. The count alone does not tell you whether the action fitted the situation.
paragraphs.zh: 如果本次较常选到这一主题，可以先想一件近来的事情，而不是直接概括人格。当时缺的是决定、愿意行动的人、信息，还是共识？提出结构可能回应其中一项需要，也可能错过另一项；次数本身不能判断当时是否合适。

title.en: A group is waiting for someone to begin
title.zh: 一群人都在等起点

paragraphs.en: Imagine several friends arranging a shared event. Everyone has preferences, but nobody has written down a first proposal. You suggest a time, a modest budget and two tasks that need owners, then ask what needs changing. Here, taking initiative means making a proposal available for discussion rather than treating silence as permission to decide for everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 比如几位朋友商量一次共同活动，人人有偏好，却没人整理第一版方案。你提出时间、小范围预算，以及两项需要分工的事情，再问哪些地方要改。这里的主动，是拿出可讨论的草案，而不是把别人没说话当作替所有人拍板的许可。

paragraphs.en: A different situation may already have a responsible organizer. Adding a second plan without checking can duplicate work or create confusion. The same urge to move things forward can then be expressed by asking what help is actually useful. A theme label does not settle who has authority in a real group.
paragraphs.zh: 另一种情况是现场已有负责组织的人。没核对就再加一套安排，可能重复劳动或造成混乱。相同的推进愿望，此时也可以表现为先问到底需要哪种帮助。一个主题标签不能决定现实群体里谁有决定权。

title.en: Movement can clarify, and it can rush
title.zh: 推进既可能厘清，也可能催快

paragraphs.en: A visible next step can help people discover where they agree and what information is missing. A short proposal is especially different from a demand when others can reject or revise it. Look for evidence that the shared task became clearer; do not assume initiative itself is always a contribution.
paragraphs.zh: 一个可见的下一步，有时能让大家发现哪些地方一致、还缺什么信息。允许别人否决或修改时，简短提案才更像提案，而不是命令。可以看共同任务是否真的更清楚，而不要预设只要主动就一定是在贡献。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears when speed leaves too little room for another person’s constraint. A deadline you suggest may not be feasible, and a role you find obvious may require consent or expertise. If disagreement appears, it is information about the arrangement, not proof that others are unmotivated or that you must push harder.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在速度挤掉了他人限制的时候。你提的期限未必可行，你觉得明显的分工也可能需要对方同意或具备相应知识。出现不同意见，是关于安排的新信息，不是别人不积极、或你必须更用力推的证据。

title.en: Initiator, Action Starter and Contingency Planner
title.zh: 与先行者、预案者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Action Starter emphasizes trying a small, reversible part before a perfect plan exists. Initiator emphasizes making a shared next step explicit. You might offer structure without wanting to experiment, or start an individual trial without organizing anyone else. Neither reading is a higher level of the other.
paragraphs.zh: “先行者”偏向在完整方案出现前，先试一个可调整的小部分；“带队推进者”偏向让共同的下一步明确起来。你可以愿意组织却不想试新办法，也可以独自试验而不安排任何人；两者不是高低层级。

paragraphs.en: Contingency Planner focuses more on responsibilities, updates and backups before relying on a plan. An initiator may bring a starting point while a planner notices what it lacks. If both descriptions fit, the useful comparison is how they worked together in a specific situation, not which nickname should win permanently.
paragraphs.zh: “预案者”更关注依赖一个计划前，职责、更新和备选方案是否明确。推进者可能带来起点，预案者可能看出起点还缺什么。两种描述都像自己时，更值得比较它们怎样在具体事情里配合，而不是让哪个昵称永久胜出。

title.en: Offer a draft with an explicit invitation
title.zh: 把可修改的草案拿出来

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes shared task, try a proposal with three parts: the next action, what you are volunteering to do and what still needs agreement. For example: “I can draft the list tonight. Would this date work, and is anything important missing?” That keeps the offer observable without claiming a general leadership trait.
paragraphs.zh: 在一件低风险共同任务里，可以试着把提案拆成三部分：下一步是什么、自己愿意做什么、什么仍需商量。比如：“今晚我可以先列清单。这个日期适合吗，有没有漏掉的重要事？”这样能观察一项具体提议，不必先给自己认领领导特质。

paragraphs.en: Check whether others could disagree or change the proposal without needing to defend themselves. If not, reduce the size of the decision or ask one genuine question before continuing. Success here means learning what the group needs, not persuading everyone or proving that an Initiator result was accurate.
paragraphs.zh: 之后可以核对：别人是否能不同意或修改，而不必先为自己辩护？如果不能，可以缩小决定范围，或先真诚地问一个问题。这里的目标是弄清群体需要什么，不是说服所有人，也不是证明这次标签很准。

title.en: No job-fit, power or competence score
title.zh: 不据此判断职业、权力或能力

paragraphs.en: The historical BOSS theme supplies the name lineage, not evidence of management ability or suitability for authority. This revised Web bank gives one count for each literal choice, preserves ties and publishes the method. Four comparisons against particular themes cannot establish performance, a career match or a complete ranking of personality.
paragraphs.zh: 旧BOSS主题提供的是名称脉络，不是管理能力或适合掌权的证据。网页修订题本按实际选择加一次、保留并列，并公开方法。与特定主题比较四次，不能建立工作表现、职业匹配或人格的完整排序。

paragraphs.en: Use the guide as an optional language for discussing a recent action. You can read every other theme for free without producing another result or sharing this one. For a real team decision, rely on relevant responsibilities, demonstrated work, agreement and context rather than a playful label.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以把指南当作讨论近期行动的可选语言。其他主题也都能直接免费阅读，不必再做出一个结果或分享本次结果。现实团队作决定时，应看相应职责、实际工作、共识和情境，而不是依赖一个趣味标签。

title.en: Caregiver: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 照应者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Caregiver refers to choices about asking how someone is doing, noticing when a participant lacks information and offering to listen before solving. In the fifty-choice edition, these are editorial examples of care in ordinary interaction. A count does not show that you can read someone’s needs without asking or that you are responsible for meeting them.

title.en: Attention to comfort and participation
title.zh: 关注舒适与参与

paragraphs.en: Caregiver refers to choices about asking how someone is doing, noticing when a participant lacks information and offering to listen before solving. In the fifty-choice edition, these are editorial examples of care in ordinary interaction. A count does not show that you can read someone’s needs without asking or that you are responsible for meeting them.
paragraphs.zh: “照应者”指向询问近况、留意参与者是否缺信息、提出办法前先愿意听一听等选择。在五十题版里，它们只是日常互动中关于照应的编辑性例子。次数不能说明你不用问就能知道他人需要什么，也不表示你负责满足那些需要。

paragraphs.en: The source nickname MUM is not used to assign a gender, family role or caregiving duty. People of different genders and circumstances may recognize some of these actions. You may also prefer a direct, practical response in another situation. The label is a way to inspect a few choices, not a test of how caring a person is.
paragraphs.zh: 源昵称MUM不用于分配性别、家庭角色或照顾义务。不同性别、不同处境的人都可能认得其中一些行动；换个情境，你也可能更愿意直接处理实际问题。标签只是帮助检查几次选择，不是衡量一个人够不够关心别人。

title.en: A quiet person at a gathering
title.zh: 聚会里安静下来的人

paragraphs.en: Imagine a friend becoming quieter during a gathering. You could assume they are upset, fill the silence for them or ask a simple question: “Would you like a break, company or neither?” The third approach leaves room for an answer you did not predict. The friend may be tired, absorbed in something else or simply enjoying listening.
paragraphs.zh: 比如聚会时，一位朋友逐渐安静。你可以猜对方不开心、替对方把沉默填满，也可以简单问：“想休息一下、有人陪着，还是都不用？”第三种问法，给没预料到的回答留了空间。朋友也可能只是累了、在想别的事，或正享受听别人说话。

paragraphs.en: Care can then mean accepting “I am fine” rather than escalating attention. In a shared task, the equivalent might be checking whether someone received the instructions, not deciding they need rescuing. What matters is the person’s stated need and the actual context; the quiz supplies neither of those facts.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，照应也可能意味着接受一句“我没事”，而不是继续加码关注。放到共同任务里，类似动作可能是确认对方收到说明没有，而不是认定对方需要被拯救。重要的是本人说出的需要和实际情境；游戏并不提供这两项事实。

title.en: Support can become an assumed duty
title.zh: 支持也可能变成默认义务

paragraphs.en: A relevant check-in can make an invitation or a task easier to understand. Asking before offering advice may also reveal that listening is wanted instead of a solution. These are possible uses of a specific action, not abilities established by selecting a response in a quiz.
paragraphs.zh: 合适的确认，有时能让一次邀请或任务更容易被理解。给建议之前先问，也可能发现对方想要的是有人听，而不是一套解决方案。这是某项行动可能产生的用途，不是选了一个选项就证明的能力。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears if you become the default monitor of everyone’s comfort while your own needs go unspoken. It can also appear when an offer is hard to refuse. Check capacity and consent on both sides. Caring about a person does not create an unlimited obligation to be available, solve the problem or stay in an unsafe situation.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在你成了所有人舒适程度的默认监测员，自己的需要却一直没说；也可能出现在一个好意让人难以拒绝。可以同时核对双方的余力与意愿。在乎一个人，不会自动产生无限在线、解决问题或留在不安全处境里的义务。

title.en: Caregiver, Giver and Appreciator
title.zh: 与付出者、记好者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Giver emphasizes offering time, effort or another practical resource. Caregiver emphasizes checking how participation or an interaction feels and what support is wanted. You can ask a thoughtful question without taking on extra work, or contribute resources without wanting a long emotional conversation. Neither action guarantees that it will help.
paragraphs.zh: “投入付出者”更强调拿出时间、力气或实际资源；“照应者”更强调确认参与和相处的状态，以及对方想要哪种支持。你可以认真问一句，却不额外接活；也可以提供资源，却不想展开很长的情绪对话。任何一种行动都不保证一定有帮助。

paragraphs.en: Appreciator emphasizes recognizing support already received and allowing room for an explanation. That differs from checking a present need. Several themes can fit the same interaction, and equal counts are allowed. They do not identify a hidden attachment style, a family history or a fixed role within a relationship.
paragraphs.zh: “记好者”更强调看见已收到的支持、给解释留位置，这与确认当下需要有所不同。同一次互动可能同时符合几个主题，并列也是允许的。它们不能识别隐藏的依恋类型、家庭经历，或你在关系里必须担任的固定角色。

title.en: Make an offer that can be declined
title.zh: 让好意能够被拒绝

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary interaction, make a small, specific offer and include a real way to decline. You might ask, “Would ten minutes of listening help, or would you rather have some quiet?” State what you can actually offer instead of promising unlimited support. The useful observation is what the person says and what happens next.
paragraphs.zh: 可以在一次普通互动里，提出一个小而具体、也真正能拒绝的帮助。比如：“听你说十分钟会有用吗，还是你更想安静一会儿？”说明自己实际能提供什么，而不是答应无限支持。值得观察的是对方怎么说，以及接下来实际发生了什么。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, check your own capacity as well. If the offer added more work than you could manage, change its scope next time. If the person preferred another kind of help, use that information rather than treating refusal as rejection of you. This is a bounded reflection, not a guarantee of better relationships.
paragraphs.zh: 事后也可以核对自己的余力。如果这个好意带来的工作超出承受范围，下次就缩小范围；如果对方更需要另一种帮助，可以使用这条信息，而不急着把拒绝理解为对自己的否定。这是有边界的观察，不保证关系一定改善。

title.en: Care is not measured by a nickname
title.zh: 关心程度不由昵称衡量

paragraphs.en: Four scheduled appearances of this theme, with two A and two B positions, contribute to a relative count. The result does not measure empathy, parenting ability, professional caregiving skill or moral worth. Different themes face different alternatives, so the numbers are not a complete comparison of twenty-five independent traits.
paragraphs.zh: 本主题按安排出现四次，A、B各两次，形成的是一项相对选择次数。结果不测共情、养育能力、专业照护技能或道德价值。不同主题遇到的替代描述不同，数字也不是二十五项独立特质的完整比较。

paragraphs.en: Every public explanation is available without another test, payment or sharing. You can finish here or compare a neighboring theme while keeping your own examples private. The historical twenty-five-theme lineage explains this edition’s vocabulary; it does not establish a validated SBTI instrument or equivalence with other websites’ question banks.
paragraphs.zh: 所有公开解释都能直接阅读，不需要再做测试、付费或分享。你可以到这里结束，也可以比较一个相邻主题，同时把个人例子留给自己。旧二十五主题脉络只解释本版的用词，不会建立一项已验证的SBTI量表，也不等于其他网站的题本。

title.en: Changing expression across settings
title.zh: 场景改变时，表达也改变

paragraphs.en: Social Adapter names choices about changing your wording, observing a new group and adjusting expression to the setting. The theme concerns how you present something, not whether your underlying intention is sincere. Its count records selections in this particular comparison schedule; it does not detect deception or establish social skill.
paragraphs.zh: “场景切换者”指向调整用词、观察新群体、随场合改变表达的选择。它关注怎样呈现一件事，不判断内心是否真诚。次数记录的只是本套比较里的选择，不能识别欺骗，也不能证明社交能力。

paragraphs.en: Someone may use formal language with a client and relaxed language with a friend while meaning exactly the same thing. Another change may feel uncomfortable or conceal an important preference. Keep those situations separate instead of using one playful nickname to explain every version of yourself.
paragraphs.zh: 一个人对客户正式些、对朋友放松些，可能表达的意思完全相同；另一次调整却可能让自己不舒服，或把重要偏好藏住。可以把这些情况分开，不用一个趣味昵称解释所有状态。

title.en: The same request, two audiences
title.zh: 同一项请求，两种听众

paragraphs.en: Imagine asking for a later meeting time. With a close friend, you might simply say you need another hour. With a new colleague, you might explain the constraint and suggest alternatives. The wording changes, but the request can remain clear in both settings. Adapting expression does not require surrendering the request itself.
paragraphs.zh: 比如想把碰面时间往后挪一小时。对熟悉的朋友，你可能直接说还需要一小时；对新同事，你可能解释限制，再给出备选时间。说法变了，两种场合里的请求仍可以同样清楚。调整表达，不必等于放弃请求本身。

paragraphs.en: The relevant question is what the other person could actually understand. If the second version becomes so polite that nobody knows a change is needed, the adaptation has a cost. If it supplies useful context without hiding the request, it may fit this conversation. The quiz cannot tell which occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 可以核对的是：对方实际能听明白什么？如果第二种说法客气到没人知道需要改时间，调整就有了代价；如果增加的是有用背景，又没藏掉请求，它可能适合这次谈话。游戏无法判断当时是哪一种。

title.en: Flexibility with a recognizable intention
title.zh: 灵活表达，也保留自己的意思

paragraphs.en: Changing examples, pace or formality can make a message easier to follow when audiences have different information. That usefulness has to be checked in the interaction. A high theme count does not prove that you understand the room, and a low count does not mean you are inconsiderate.
paragraphs.zh: 听众掌握的信息不同时，换例子、语速或正式程度，可能让话更容易被理解，但有没有用仍要放回互动中核对。次数高，不能证明你看懂了气氛；次数低，也不表示你不体谅别人。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff is losing track of what you wanted to communicate while managing how it might be received. You might agree too quickly, postpone a necessary objection or spend a long time reviewing your performance. Those possibilities are prompts for a real example, not consequences established by a result.
paragraphs.zh: 需要取舍的地方，是忙着照顾话会怎样被接收，却慢慢忘了自己想表达什么。你可能答应太快、把必要的异议往后拖，或事后花很久复盘表现。这些只是可供核对的情境，不是结果已经证实的后果。

title.en: Adapter, Expressive Styler and Caregiver
title.zh: 与表达造型者、照应者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Expressive Styler concerns giving a message or appearance a distinctive personal form. Social Adapter concerns changing that form between audiences. A carefully styled presentation can stay almost identical everywhere; an understated presentation can change substantially. Neither count measures authenticity or how others judge the result.
paragraphs.zh: “表达造型者”关注让消息或外在呈现带有个人风格；“场景切换者”关注这种呈现随听众发生的改变。精心设计的风格可能到哪里都差不多，不显眼的说法也可能变化很大。两项次数都不测真实性或他人的评价。

paragraphs.en: Caregiver concerns checking another person’s need or participation. You can adapt a message without taking responsibility for everyone’s comfort, and you can offer care while speaking in your usual way. Overlap is expected in an editorial theme game; these are not separate clinical categories.
paragraphs.zh: “照应者”关注确认他人的需要或参与状态。你可以换一种讲法，却不负责所有人的舒适；也可以关心别人，同时保持惯常的表达。在编辑性主题游戏里，重叠很正常，它们不是互相排斥的临床类别。

title.en: Keep one sentence constant
title.zh: 留住一句不变的意思

paragraphs.en: For an ordinary request, write one sentence stating what you mean before deciding how to say it. Then adapt the explanation for the listener. For example, keep “I cannot take this on this week” constant while changing the amount of background. The aim is clarity, not proving a type.
paragraphs.zh: 可以为一个普通请求先写一句“我到底是什么意思”，再决定怎样向对方解释。比如保留“这周我接不了这件事”，根据听众改变背景说明的多少。目的是让话更清楚，而不是证明自己属于哪一型。

paragraphs.en: After the conversation, compare the understood request with that original sentence. If they differ, a short clarification may be more useful than judging the whole interaction as a performance. If they match, you need not keep polishing it. This optional reflection does not promise confidence or social approval.
paragraphs.zh: 谈完后，可以比较对方理解到的请求和最初那句话。如果不同，一次简短澄清可能比把整场对话当表演评分更有用；如果一致，也不必一直打磨。这项可选观察不保证获得自信或他人好感。

title.en: A source nickname is not a verdict
title.zh: 源昵称不是对人的判决

paragraphs.en: The historical FAKE theme is the provenance link; this edition does not call you fake or nonhuman. Four appearances, with two A and two B positions, contribute to a relative count against four scheduled alternatives. The count is neither a lie detector nor a complete ordering of twenty-five personality traits.
paragraphs.zh: 旧FAKE主题只是溯源脉络，本版不据此说你虚假或不像人。本主题出现四次，A、B各两次，与安排好的四种替代描述比较后得到相对次数。它既不是测谎，也不是二十五种人格特质的完整排序。

paragraphs.en: You may reject the label, compare other free guides or finish here. Public explanations contain no personal answers or counts. Do not use this result to judge a partner’s honesty, make employment decisions or explain someone else’s history. A playful response record cannot establish those facts.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以不接受这个标签，比较其他免费指南，也可以读完结束。公开解释不含个人回答或次数。不要用本结果评判伴侣是否诚实、作招聘决定，或解释别人的经历；一份趣味选择记录建立不了这些事实。

It records selected descriptions of engagement. It does not establish that you have lost interest in life, lack emotion or see through things more accurately than others.
summary.zh: “抽离观察者”指向先问目标是否有意义、站在名次竞争的边缘，以及不加入每项被说成必不可少的活动。它记录的是几种投入方式的选择，不说明你失去生活兴趣、没有情绪，或比别人更能看透事情。

title.en: Stepping back from a ready-made meaning
title.zh: 先退一步，看意义是否属于自己

paragraphs.en: Detached Observer names choices about questioning a goal’s meaning, staying outside a status contest and not joining every activity described as essential. It records selected descriptions of engagement. It does not establish that you have lost interest in life, lack emotion or see through things more accurately than others.
paragraphs.zh: “抽离观察者”指向先问目标是否有意义、站在名次竞争的边缘，以及不加入每项被说成必不可少的活动。它记录的是几种投入方式的选择，不说明你失去生活兴趣、没有情绪，或比别人更能看透事情。

paragraphs.en: A theme can resemble one recent context while missing another. You may step back from a competition and become deeply involved in a personal project. Keep the object of your interest visible. The quiz cannot turn a selective response in one month into an explanation of your whole life.
paragraphs.zh: 这个主题可能像最近的一种情境，却不像另一种。你可以退出一次竞争，同时很投入自己的项目。可以把“究竟对什么投入”保留下来，游戏不能把一个月里有所选择的反应，变成对整个人生的解释。

title.en: An invitation everyone says you must accept
title.zh: 别人说非参加不可的邀请

paragraphs.en: Imagine being invited to an event because “everyone important will be there.” You are not immediately convinced. You might ask what will actually happen, whether you want those conversations and what attending would cost. Stepping back creates space to decide, but does not make attending shallow or declining wise.
paragraphs.zh: 比如有人邀你参加活动，理由是“重要的人都会去”。你没有马上被说服，想先问实际会发生什么、是否想进行那些交流，以及参加要付出什么。退一步可以给决定留空间，但不会使参加显得肤浅，或使拒绝自动显得明智。

paragraphs.en: A different invitation may concern something you value directly. In that case, distance can give way to participation without contradicting a permanent identity. Look at what changed in the information or your priorities. A count cannot tell whether a particular decision was avoidance, discernment or simply an ordinary preference.
paragraphs.zh: 换一份邀请，如果内容本身就是你在意的事，抽离也可以转为参与，不必担心违背一个永久身份。可以看看信息或优先顺序发生了什么变化。次数不能判断某次决定是逃避、辨别，还是一种普通偏好。

title.en: Space to choose, and the chance of staying outside
title.zh: 留下选择空间，也可能一直在场外

paragraphs.en: Questioning a ready-made goal can help separate your own reasons from expectations you have inherited. The practical value lies in the reason you eventually identify, not in maintaining distance for its own sake. This guide does not claim that detachment produces clearer judgment or a superior perspective.
paragraphs.zh: 问一问现成目标，可以帮助区分自己的理由和接过来的期待。实际价值在于最后辨认出了什么理由，而不是为了抽离而保持抽离。这份指南不声称距离会带来更清晰的判断或更优越的视角。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff can appear if every possible activity is dismissed before you learn enough to choose. Some useful experiences begin without a grand purpose. You can inspect one small opportunity without committing to its whole story. Whether that is worthwhile depends on your circumstances, not on a theme result.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在还没了解多少，就把每个活动都否定的时候。有些有用体验并不以宏大意义开场。你可以只看看一个小机会，不必连它的整套叙事都接受。值不值得，取决于现实处境，而不是主题结果。

title.en: Observer, Quiet Observer and Pause Taker
title.zh: 与静观者、休眠者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Quiet Observer concerns enjoying enoughness and time without visible achievement. Detached Observer concerns stepping back from particular claims about what should matter. You can value quiet while eagerly joining a cause, or question a cause while enjoying a busy social life. Similar wording does not make their examples interchangeable.
paragraphs.zh: “静观者”关注觉得已经足够，以及不必产出明显成果的时间；“抽离观察者”关注与某些“什么才重要”的说法拉开距离。你可以喜欢安静，却很愿意参加一件事；也可以质疑一种目标，同时享受热闹生活。字面相似不表示例子可以互换。

paragraphs.en: Pause Taker concerns an interval before responding or restarting a task. An interval can be practical without any question about meaning. Neither label identifies depression, burnout, a reason for exhaustion or a personal history. If several descriptions fit, compare the actual situations rather than assigning a cause.
paragraphs.zh: “休眠者”关注回应或重启任务之前的一段间隔。有时只是需要缓一缓，并不涉及意义问题。两个标签都不能识别抑郁、倦怠、疲惫原因或个人经历。几种描述都像自己时，可以比较具体场面，而不是直接指定一个原因。

title.en: Name the smallest reason that matters
title.zh: 找一个足够具体的小理由

paragraphs.en: Choose an ordinary invitation or task and complete two sentences: “The reason offered to me is…” and “My reason for joining or declining is….” They may match. If they do not, you can keep the distinction without deciding that either side is foolish. No big statement about your purpose is required.
paragraphs.zh: 可以选一项普通邀请或任务，补完两句话：“别人给出的理由是……”以及“我参加或拒绝的理由是……”。两者可以相同；不同的时候，也可以保留差别，不必先判断哪一方愚蠢。这里不需要给自己的人生目标作大声明。

paragraphs.en: If you are unsure, identify one piece of information or one limited experience that could help. You can also decline without performing an experiment. The purpose is to make a real choice more legible, not to prove you are detached or force yourself to become enthusiastic.
paragraphs.zh: 如果还不确定，可以找出一条可能有帮助的信息，或一个范围有限的体验；你也可以不试就拒绝。目的是更看得清一项真实选择，不是证明自己够抽离，也不是强迫自己兴奋起来。

title.en: No health or life-meaning conclusion
title.zh: 不据此判断健康或人生状态

paragraphs.en: This edition uses the historical DEAD theme as lineage while removing literal death and rarity claims from the reading. Its four comparisons do not measure health, motivation, emotional capacity or how meaningful your life is. Different opponents and editorial examples limit what can be inferred from counts, even when one label is highest.
paragraphs.zh: 本版沿用旧DEAD主题的脉络，但不采用字面死亡或稀有度说法。四组比较不测健康、动机、情感能力，也不判断你的人生有没有意义。即使某个标签次数最高，不同对手与编辑性例子仍严格限制了能够推断什么。

paragraphs.en: The full guide is available without answering, sharing or taking another test. You may stop if this vocabulary feels unhelpful. Actual persistent difficulties need to be understood through their own context; a playful label neither explains them nor decides what support you should seek.
paragraphs.zh: 不作答、不分享、不再做其他测评，也能读完这份指南。如果这些用词没帮助，你可以结束。现实中持续的困难需要按其自身情境去理解；趣味标签不能解释它们，也不能决定你该寻找哪种支持。

title.en: An interval before returning
title.zh: 回到事情之前的一段间隔

paragraphs.en: Pause Taker refers to choices about wanting a quiet interval, asking for time and restarting through a short uninterrupted work block. These are descriptions of pacing. They do not establish laziness, poor reliability, a medical need for rest or a general inability to respond.
paragraphs.zh: “休眠者”指向想要一段安静、说明需要时间，或靠一小段不受打扰的工作重新启动等选择。这是关于节奏的描述，不说明懒惰、不可靠、医学上的休息需要，或普遍没有回应能力。

paragraphs.en: A pause can have different meanings depending on what has been agreed. Taking space after a voluntary conversation differs from leaving someone without information they need for a shared commitment. Use a recent example and its actual expectations rather than treating all delayed responses as the same behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 暂停的意思取决于双方原先约定了什么。自愿聊天后留一点空间，与共同承诺中让对方拿不到必要信息，并不是一件事。可以带着最近的例子和实际期待来理解，而不把所有延迟回应都算作同一种行为。

title.en: Messages arrive while attention is already full
title.zh: 注意力已满，消息又来了

paragraphs.en: Imagine several messages arriving while you are finishing a demanding task. You want to step away from the conversation. One option is a brief, accurate update: “I have seen this and can reply tomorrow.” That creates a different arrangement from promising an immediate answer while hoping the messages will disappear.
paragraphs.zh: 比如正在完成一件费神的事，几条消息又接着进来，你想先离开对话。一种做法是简短而准确地更新：“我看到了，明天可以回复。”这与先答应马上回答、心里却希望消息自己消失，是不同的安排。

paragraphs.en: The right response depends on urgency and responsibility. An ordinary chat may need no schedule; a time-sensitive shared task may need a handoff. The theme does not excuse missed obligations or require constant availability. It simply gives you a place to inspect how space and expectations were negotiated.
paragraphs.zh: 具体怎么回应，要看紧急程度与职责。普通闲聊未必需要日程，受期限约束的共同任务却可能需要交接。主题既不为失约开脱，也不要求随时在线，只是让你有一个入口，看看空间和期待当时怎样被协商。

title.en: A pause that has a return point
title.zh: 有返回点的暂停

paragraphs.en: A bounded interval can make it easier to decide what you are actually ready to say or do. Check that possibility against an example: did the pause supply space or information, and was the next step clearer? A quiz selection alone does not show that taking a break helped.
paragraphs.zh: 有边界的间隔，有时能让你更清楚自己准备好说什么、做什么。可以带着例子核对：这段暂停是否带来了空间或信息，下一步是否更清楚？仅仅选过一个选项，不能说明暂停确实有帮助。

paragraphs.en: The cost can appear when a pause has no return point and the unresolved task keeps growing. It can also appear when a return time is unrealistically short. You may need to change the agreement, reduce the task or ask for help. None of those choices is determined by having this nickname.
paragraphs.zh: 代价可能出现在暂停没有返回点、未处理事情越积越多的时候，也可能出现在答应的返回时间过短。你可能需要改约定、缩小任务，或请人帮助；这些选择都不是由昵称替你决定的。

title.en: Pause Taker, Low-Battery Rebuilder and Independent Walker
title.zh: 与低电量整备者、独行者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Low-Battery Rebuilder emphasizes reducing a load and finding a manageable next step when energy feels limited. Pause Taker emphasizes the interval itself and how a task or conversation restarts. Either description may fit without the other. The scores do not quantify energy, recovery or the reason for a difficult day.
paragraphs.zh: “低电量整备者”更关注精力有限时减一点负担、找一个做得到的步骤；“休眠者”更关注间隔本身，以及任务或对话怎样重启。一个描述可以符合，另一个未必符合。次数不量化精力、恢复程度或一天难过的原因。

paragraphs.en: Independent Walker concerns choosing to handle something alone or sorting a feeling privately. You can want company after a pause, or work independently without needing a pause. These editorial themes may overlap, and ties do not indicate a hidden condition or a failure to find your real type.
paragraphs.zh: “独行者”关注先独自处理事情，或私下整理感受。你可以暂停后希望有人陪，也可以一直独立做事而不需要暂停。编辑性主题可以重叠，并列不说明有某种隐藏情况，也不表示没找到真正的类型。

title.en: Try a smaller return agreement
title.zh: 试一个更小的返回约定

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary task, choose a small return point that you can check: opening the document, answering one question or deciding whether more time is needed. If another person depends on it, communicate the arrangement. The aim is a usable agreement, not performing productivity to satisfy a result.
paragraphs.zh: 可以为一件普通任务选一个能核对的小返回点：打开文档、回答一个问题，或决定是否还需要时间。如果有人依赖这件事，也把安排告诉对方。目标是得到可用的约定，不是为了符合结果而表演高效率。

paragraphs.en: After returning, notice whether the task is clearer or whether the obstacle remains. A missing instruction, excessive workload or competing responsibility may need a different response. Keep those facts visible instead of interpreting every difficult restart as a fixed personality feature. You are free not to use this exercise.
paragraphs.zh: 回来后，可以看看任务是否更清楚，还是障碍仍在。缺少说明、负担过多或职责相互冲突，可能需要不同处理。可以保留这些事实，而不把每次难启动都解释为固定人格特征；你也完全可以不做这项练习。

title.en: A playful label for four comparisons
title.zh: 四组比较里的一个趣味标签

paragraphs.en: The historical ZZZZ nickname is the source lineage, not a finding about sleep, burnout or reliability. This theme appears four times, twice in each position, against particular alternatives. Counts are relative to that schedule and do not provide a complete ranking of twenty-five independent traits or a recommended amount of rest.
paragraphs.zh: 旧ZZZZ昵称提供的是来源脉络，不是关于睡眠、倦怠或可靠性的发现。本主题出现四次，两个位置各两次，与特定替代描述比较。次数依赖这套安排，既不是二十五项独立特质的完整排序，也不会给出推荐休息量。

paragraphs.en: You can read all explanations before answering and leave without generating a result. Personal responses follow the stated memory-only controls; public guides contain no private counts. A real responsibility or persistent difficulty should be discussed on its own facts, not settled by a nickname.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以先看所有解释，也可以不生成结果就离开。私人回答按页面说明只留在内存，公开指南没有个人次数。现实中的职责或持续困难，应按自身事实讨论，而不是交给一个昵称来裁定。

summary.zh: “先行者”指向先试一个能承担的小部分、拿出初稿、收到反馈后再调整等选择。它关注普通、可调整任务怎样开始。次数不测勇气、速度、能力，也不判断是否愿意承担重大风险。一个实际例子，比认领标签更重要。

title.en: A small attempt before a perfect plan
title.zh: 完整方案之前的一小次尝试

paragraphs.en: Action Starter names choices about trying a manageable part, producing a first draft and adjusting after feedback. It concerns how you might begin an ordinary, reversible task. The count does not measure courage, speed, competence or willingness to take serious risks. A practical example matters more than accepting the label.
paragraphs.zh: “先行者”指向先试一个能承担的小部分、拿出初稿、收到反馈后再调整等选择。它关注普通、可调整任务怎样开始。次数不测勇气、速度、能力，也不判断是否愿意承担重大风险。一个实际例子，比认领标签更重要。

paragraphs.en: You may recognize this approach when learning a hobby but prefer a complete plan for travel or shared responsibilities. That difference is useful information. Choosing one description over another in this game cannot establish a general rule for every decision you face.
paragraphs.zh: 学一项兴趣活动时，你可能认得这种做法；安排行程或共同职责时，却更想先有完整计划。这种差别本身就有信息。游戏里更偏向一条描述，不能建立适用于每个决定的一般规则。

title.en: A rough draft that answers one question
title.zh: 用粗稿回答一个问题

paragraphs.en: Imagine wanting to make a short presentation. Instead of polishing the whole outline, you sketch one slide to see whether the central example is understandable. The trial has a limited question and a small cost. It is different from publishing an unchecked presentation or assuming preparation is unnecessary.
paragraphs.zh: 比如想做一份简短演示。你没有先把整份提纲打磨完，而是画一页粗稿，看看核心例子能不能让人理解。这个尝试的问题范围有限，代价也小；它不同于把未核对的内容直接公开，也不表示准备工作没有必要。

paragraphs.en: After someone reviews the slide, you may discover that the example works but the sequence does not. The next action can then be a revision rather than another leap. A useful attempt can change your plan or show that continuing is not worthwhile. The theme does not require relentless action.
paragraphs.zh: 请人看过后，你可能发现例子能用，顺序却不合适，下一步因而是修改，而不是再往前冲。有用的尝试可以改变计划，也可以告诉你继续并不值得。这个主题不要求始终保持行动。

title.en: Learning by doing needs a boundary
title.zh: 边做边看，也需要边界

paragraphs.en: A small trial may reveal details that were difficult to imagine in advance. Check what information it actually supplied. Did you learn about the task, the materials or your interest? The quiz cannot establish that acting sooner produced a better outcome, and more attempts are not automatically more informative.
paragraphs.zh: 小试一次，可能看见事前难以想象的细节。可以核对它实际提供了什么信息：关于任务、材料，还是自己的兴趣？游戏不能证明早行动就有更好结果，尝试次数更多，也不自动表示信息更多。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff changes when an action is costly, hard to reverse or affects people who have not agreed. A playful preference is no reason to bypass necessary preparation or safety checks. Keep the size of the experiment proportionate to what is at stake, and accept that some decisions need expertise before action.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦行动代价大、难以回头，或会影响尚未同意的人，取舍就变了。趣味偏好不是跳过必要准备或安全核对的理由。可以让尝试的规模与后果相称，也承认有些决定需要先取得专业信息。

title.en: Action Starter, Initiator and Improviser
title.zh: 与推进者、灵活应对者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Initiator concerns making a shared next step explicit and inviting agreement. Action Starter concerns learning through a first attempt. A person can organize carefully without wanting an early experiment, or run a private trial without coordinating a group. These are different examples, not levels of leadership.
paragraphs.zh: “带队推进者”关注明确共同的下一步，并邀请大家商量；“先行者”关注从初次尝试中获得信息。一个人可以很愿意组织，却不想提早试验；也可以独自试一下，而不协调群体。它们是不同例子，不是领导力的层级。

paragraphs.en: Improviser concerns rearranging what is available after conditions change. You might prefer early action when circumstances are stable and still dislike frequent changes. Or you might adapt readily after a plan is disrupted while preferring a slower start. Equal or different counts cannot decide which response is better.
paragraphs.zh: “灵活应对者”更关注条件改变后，怎样重新使用手头的东西。你可能愿意在稳定情境里早点开始，却不喜欢不断变化；也可能起步谨慎，但计划被打断后很能调整。次数相同或不同，都不能裁定哪一种更好。

title.en: Define what a trial is for
title.zh: 先说清试这一下为了什么

paragraphs.en: For an optional, low-stakes task, name the question, the smallest attempt and a stopping point. For example: “I want to know whether this layout is readable; show one rough page to one reader; decide afterward whether to revise.” The purpose is to gather relevant information, not to demonstrate an energetic identity.
paragraphs.zh: 可以为一件自愿、低风险的小事，写下要回答的问题、最小尝试和停止点。比如：“我想知道排版是否易读；给一位读者看一页粗稿；之后再决定是否修改。”目的是获得相关信息，不是证明自己属于很有冲劲的一类人。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, distinguish what the attempt showed from what remains unknown. One reader’s response is not everyone’s response; one successful attempt is not general ability. You can enlarge, change or abandon the next step. This reflection offers no promise of productivity, confidence or success.
paragraphs.zh: 事后可以区分：这次试出了什么，什么还不知道？一个读者的反应不是所有人的反应，一次顺利也不是普遍能力。下一步可以扩大、改变，也可以放下。这项观察不保证效率、自信或成功。

title.en: No measure of bravery or achievement
title.zh: 不测勇敢程度或成就

paragraphs.en: The historical GOGO theme supplies the lineage for this revised reading. The new bank uses fifty paired choices; this theme appears four times, twice in each position. Different themes meet different alternatives. A higher count is not proof that you are more decisive, adventurous or effective than another person.
paragraphs.zh: 本修订读法沿用旧GOGO主题的脉络。新题本有五十组成对选择，本主题出现四次，两个位置各两次；不同主题遇到的替代描述不同。次数更高，不证明你比别人更果断、更敢冒险或更有效。

paragraphs.en: All explanations remain free and can be read without answering. Public pages contain no personal responses or counts. Use actual task requirements for important decisions; neither this nickname nor another entertainment result supplies permission, qualification or evidence that a consequential action is appropriate.
paragraphs.zh: 所有解释都免费开放，不作答也能阅读。公开页不含个人回答或次数。重要决定应看实际任务要求；这个昵称或其他娱乐结果，都不能提供许可、资格，或证明一项后果重大的行动合适。

summary.zh: “直抒压力者”指向要求堆积时说出不舒服、提出暂停，或说明承受范围等描述。它关注具体情境中的表达，不判断压力、愤怒或攻击性的强度，也不证明你准确理解了别人的行为。

title.en: Putting strain into words
title.zh: 把吃不消说出来

paragraphs.en: Pressure Speaker refers to choosing descriptions of stating discomfort, asking for a pause and naming a limit when demands build up. It concerns expression during a specific situation. It does not establish the intensity of stress, anger, aggression or how accurately you understand another person’s behavior.
paragraphs.zh: “直抒压力者”指向要求堆积时说出不舒服、提出暂停，或说明承受范围等描述。它关注具体情境中的表达，不判断压力、愤怒或攻击性的强度，也不证明你准确理解了别人的行为。

paragraphs.en: A direct statement can be careful, abrupt, welcome or poorly timed depending on what happens around it. The result cannot choose among those possibilities. Start with the words you actually used, what was being asked and the response you received, rather than treating a nickname as an explanation of the whole exchange.
paragraphs.zh: 直接的一句话，可以是谨慎的、突然的、受欢迎的，也可以时机不合适，要看前后发生了什么。结果不能替你分辨。可以先看实际说了什么、当时被要求什么、对方怎样回应，而不是用昵称解释整场交流。

title.en: Another request lands on a full afternoon
title.zh: 已经排满的下午，又加了一件事

paragraphs.en: Imagine someone asking for another task when your afternoon is already committed. “I cannot finish both today; which should take priority?” names a constraint and opens a practical question. It differs from an insult, a threat or a claim that the other person should already know your limits.
paragraphs.zh: 比如下午已经排满，对方又加一件事。“今天这两件做不完，哪一件优先？”说出一个限制，也打开了实际问题。它不同于辱骂、威胁，或认定对方本来就应该知道自己的界限。

paragraphs.en: The answer may reveal a misunderstanding, an urgent need or a workload problem. You may still disagree after hearing it. A meaningful next step could be clarifying the arrangement or ending the discussion, depending on the context. The quiz cannot determine a real obligation or whether a setting is safe.
paragraphs.zh: 回答可能揭示误会、紧急需要，或工作量本身的问题。听完之后，你仍可以不同意。根据情境，下一步可能是澄清安排，也可能是结束谈话；游戏不能裁定真实义务，也不能判断现场是否安全。

title.en: A clear limit and its delivery
title.zh: 界限本身，与界限怎样表达

paragraphs.en: Naming a constraint may supply information that others did not have. Its value depends on whether the information is relevant and understandable, not on how intense the statement feels. A high count does not certify honesty, courage or good boundaries. A quiet response can also communicate a limit clearly.
paragraphs.zh: 说出限制，可能提供别人原先不知道的信息。有没有价值，要看信息是否相关、是否能被理解，而不是看说得多强烈。次数高不认证诚实、勇敢或界限良好；平静的回应也可以把限制讲清楚。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears when urgency in your delivery obscures the actual request or leaves no room for another person’s answer. That does not remove your right to refuse. You can separate the boundary from the way it was conveyed, and decide whether clarification is useful without withdrawing a legitimate limit.
paragraphs.zh: 需要取舍的地方，是表达里的急迫盖住了实际请求，或不给对方回答的空间。这不会取消你拒绝的权利。可以把界限本身和表达方式分开，判断是否需要澄清，而不必因此收回合理限制。

title.en: Pressure Speaker, Venting Fixer and Commentator
title.zh: 与吐槽补位者、鲜活反应者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Venting Fixer combines voicing frustration with taking on a particular repair or contribution. Pressure Speaker does not necessarily include taking on the task afterward. You can say that a demand is too much without agreeing to solve it. The theme does not make helping a condition for being heard.
paragraphs.zh: “吐槽补位者”把说出不满与接住一项具体修补或贡献放在一起；“直抒压力者”不一定包含之后继续承担任务。你可以说明要求太多，却不答应解决它。这个主题不把帮忙当作意见能被听见的前提。

paragraphs.en: Surprised Commentator concerns an animated reaction to something unexpected, which can be delightful as well as frustrating. These examples may overlap in a conversation but do not measure the same circumstance. A tie is not evidence of emotional instability, and no result establishes a cause for your reactions.
paragraphs.zh: “鲜活反应者”关注遇到意外时显露的反应，事情可能开心，也可能令人烦躁。两种例子会在一次谈话里重叠，却不是同一种情境。并列不说明情绪不稳定，任何结果也都不能建立反应的原因。

title.en: Say what needs to change
title.zh: 把需要改变什么说具体

paragraphs.en: For an ordinary, safe disagreement, distinguish the situation, your limit and the requested change. An example is: “The request arrived after today’s work was agreed; I cannot add it without moving something; can we choose what will wait?” This is one possible wording to inspect, not a required script or a conflict-resolution guarantee.
paragraphs.zh: 在普通、安全的分歧中，可以区分情况、自己的限制，以及希望改变什么。比如：“今天的工作已经约好后，又来了新要求；不挪动别的事就加不进来；我们能否决定哪件往后放？”这是可供观察的一种说法，不是必用话术，也不保证解决冲突。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, check whether the actual constraint became clearer. If the problem persists because responsibility or workload is unclear, address that issue rather than treating your delivery as the entire cause. If talking is unsafe or unwanted, the quiz does not require you to continue an exchange.
paragraphs.zh: 事后可以核对，实际限制是否更清楚了。如果问题持续，是因为职责或负担始终不明确，可以处理那件事，而不把全部原因都归到自己的语气。如果谈话不安全，或你不愿继续，游戏并不要求你留下来交流。

title.en: No aggression or clinical conclusion
title.zh: 不据此判断攻击性或临床状态

paragraphs.en: This edition revises the historical FUCK theme into a description of expressing strain without adopting its insulting language. Each of its four options contributes one raw count when selected. Counts have no validated threshold and do not establish a stable personality, dangerousness or the amount of pressure you are under.
paragraphs.zh: 本版把旧FUCK主题修订为关于表达吃力的描述，不采用其中的辱骂语言。四条选项被选择时各记一次原始次数，没有已验证阈值，不建立稳定人格、危险性，也不衡量你承受了多大压力。

paragraphs.en: The public guide is identical for everyone and does not reveal a private result. You can compare any other theme without retaking the quiz, sharing or signing up. Keep important judgments about behavior, obligations and safety grounded in their actual facts rather than in an entertainment label.
paragraphs.zh: 公开指南对所有人相同，不透露私人结果。无需重测、分享或注册，也能比较其他任何主题。涉及行为、义务和安全的重要判断，应回到实际事实，而不是依据娱乐标签。

title.en: Knowing what a shared plan depends on
title.zh: 弄清共同计划依赖什么

paragraphs.en: Contingency Planner names choices about clarifying responsibilities, checking a deadline’s dependencies and agreeing on updates or a backup. The theme concerns preparation around an ordinary shared arrangement. A count does not show that your predictions are accurate, that you control other people or that every detail needs a plan.
paragraphs.zh: “预案者”指向澄清分工、核对期限所依赖的条件，以及约好更新或备选办法等选择。它关注普通共同安排里的准备工作。次数不说明预测准确、不说明能控制别人，也不表示每个细节都需要计划。

paragraphs.en: You might want a clear update for a task others depend on while happily improvising a free afternoon. Context and consequence matter. The four selected examples cannot establish a general need for control, and a lower count does not prove recklessness or poor organization.
paragraphs.zh: 在别人依赖你的任务里，你可能希望更新明确；到了自由的下午，却很愿意临时起意。情境和后果都重要。四个例子不能建立普遍的控制需要，次数较低也不证明鲁莽或组织不好。

title.en: A plan changes, and a connection is missing
title.zh: 计划变了，一处衔接没跟上

paragraphs.en: Imagine a shared trip whose departure time changes. You check who will tell the others, whether a connection still works and what happens if it does not. These are specific dependencies. They differ from trying to schedule everyone’s feelings or demanding that nobody ever change a preference.
paragraphs.zh: 比如一次共同出行的出发时间改变了。你想确认谁来通知其他人、后面的衔接是否还行，以及不行时怎么办。这些是具体依赖，与替所有人安排感受，或要求任何人都不能改变偏好，不是一回事。

paragraphs.en: A short check may resolve the issue; a longer plan may add little. The relevant question is what uncertainty has a practical consequence. If you cannot identify one, it may be enough to agree on an update and leave the rest open. The result cannot determine that boundary for you.
paragraphs.zh: 短暂核对可能就能解决，也可能写更长计划仍没增加多少信息。可以问：哪个不确定因素实际会带来后果？如果说不清，也许约好一次更新、让其余部分保持开放就够了；结果不能代你画这条边界。

title.en: Preparation without an expanding checklist
title.zh: 准备不必变成无限清单

paragraphs.en: A relevant backup can make a dependency visible and give people a shared next step. Check whether it is understandable, feasible and agreed. The act of planning is not itself proof of safety, reliability or good judgment, and another person may see a constraint your plan missed.
paragraphs.zh: 相关的备选办法可以让依赖关系可见，也给大家一个共同的下一步。可以核对它是否清楚、可行，并得到同意。做了计划，本身不证明安全、可靠或判断良好；别人也可能看见计划漏掉的限制。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears when each answer generates another condition without changing the decision. A checklist can also become a way to direct people who never accepted that arrangement. Separate what needs agreement from what you would merely prefer, and allow the plan to change when new information makes it less useful.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在每个答案又引出一个条件，却始终不改变决定的时候。清单也可能变成指挥那些从未同意该安排的人的办法。可以区分必须达成共识的事和自己的偏好；新信息使计划不再适用时，也允许它改变。

title.en: Planner, Risk Watcher and Initiator
title.zh: 与预警者、推进者怎样区分

paragraphs.en: Risk Watcher emphasizes raising a possible problem or checking an uncertain claim. Contingency Planner emphasizes how an arrangement will proceed if a condition changes. You may spot a risk without wanting to organize the response, or make a backup for an ordinary known dependency without feeling worried.
paragraphs.zh: “预警者”更关注提出可能的问题，或核对不确定说法；“预案者”更关注条件改变后，安排具体怎样继续。你可以看出风险，却不想组织回应；也可以为普通、已知的依赖准备备选，而不感到担忧。

paragraphs.en: Initiator emphasizes putting a starting proposal into a shared discussion. A planner may help make that proposal usable, but planning does not give either person authority over the group. These themes can coexist. Their raw counts cannot establish management ability or a hierarchy between people.
paragraphs.zh: “带队推进者”更关注把一个起步提案放进共同讨论；预案者可能帮助它变得可用，但做计划不会让任何一方自动获得对群体的决定权。两个主题可以并存，原始次数不能建立管理能力或人与人之间的等级。

title.en: Choose one consequential uncertainty
title.zh: 只选一个有实际后果的不确定点

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes plan, identify a dependency, who needs the information and one fallback. For example: “If the room is unavailable, we will use this alternative; I will confirm it by noon.” Keep the proposal small enough for everyone affected to understand and question.
paragraphs.zh: 可以在一个低风险计划中，找一项依赖、需要知道信息的人，以及一个备选办法。比如：“如果房间不能用，就换这个地点；中午前由我确认。”把提案保持在受影响的人都能理解、也能提出疑问的范围里。

paragraphs.en: After using it, ask whether the fallback changed anything useful or simply added work. If it was unnecessary, reduce it next time. If a missing agreement was the real issue, address that rather than creating more checklists. This optional reflection does not promise better outcomes or eliminate uncertainty.
paragraphs.zh: 用过之后，可以问：备选方案带来了什么实际用途，还是只增加了工作？不需要的，下次可以减少；真正问题若是缺少共识，就处理共识，而不继续加清单。这项可选观察不保证结果更好，也不会消除不确定性。

title.en: Not a finding that you control a situation
title.zh: 不说明局面已被控制

paragraphs.en: The historical CTRL theme provides the source lineage. This revised bank uses four appearances of each theme, two in each position, with different scheduled opponents. Counts are not control scores, clinical measures or a complete ordering of twenty-five traits. A tie is a valid response pattern, not a problem to correct.
paragraphs.zh: 旧CTRL主题提供来源脉络。修订题本让每个主题出现四次，两个位置各两次，面对不同的固定比较对象。次数不是控制程度分数、临床测量，也不是二十五项特质的完整排序。并列是允许出现的选择模式，不是需要纠正的问题。

paragraphs.en: Every theme guide is free before or after answering. Public links contain no personal count or answer sheet. For decisions involving real authority, money, safety or another person’s consent, use the relevant facts and requirements. A playful planning label cannot supply approval or replace those checks.
paragraphs.zh: 作答前后，每份主题指南都可免费阅读。公开链接不包含个人次数或答卷。涉及真实权限、金钱、安全或他人同意的决定，应使用相应事实与要求；一个趣味计划标签不能提供批准，也不能代替必要核对。

title.en: Finding room for a little fun
title.zh: 给一点小乐趣留位置

paragraphs.en: Lightener refers to looking for a gentle joke, finding an amusing detail in a minor mishap, or adding play to an ordinary errand. It describes these particular choices, not a measured sense of humor. A larger count cannot tell whether other people found a joke funny or welcome.
paragraphs.zh: “轻松找乐者”指找一句温和玩笑、在小岔子里发现好笑细节，或给日常小事加一点趣味。它描述这些选择，不测幽默感。次数较多，不能说明别人是否觉得玩笑好笑或合适。

paragraphs.en: You might enjoy this approach with familiar friends and prefer a straightforward tone at work. You may also recognize only one of the four descriptions. Keep those differences instead of turning a brief comparison game into a demand to be cheerful everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 你可能喜欢和熟悉朋友这样相处，工作时则偏好直接表达；也可能只认得四条中的一条。请保留差异，不把短暂比较游戏变成必须处处快乐的要求。

title.en: A wrong turn on an ordinary outing
title.zh: 普通出游里走错一段路

paragraphs.en: Two friends take the wrong exit and have to walk back. Once they know the route is safe, one notices a ridiculous shop sign and shares a laugh. The fun can sit beside the practical correction: checking directions and deciding whether both people still want to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 两个朋友走错出口，需要折返。确认路线安全后，其中一人注意到一块好笑的店招，分享了这个细节。乐趣可以与实际补救并存：核对方向，再问两个人是否仍愿意继续。

paragraphs.en: If the other person is exhausted or upset, a joke may not be helpful. Asking what they need can matter more than keeping the mood light. The label gives no reason to minimize an inconvenience, mock someone, or treat a serious concern as entertainment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方已经疲惫或难受，玩笑可能没有帮助。问问需要什么，可以比活跃气氛更重要。标签不能成为淡化麻烦、嘲笑别人或把严肃困扰当娱乐的理由。

title.en: Play can be offered, not required
title.zh: 可以邀请玩乐，无需强求

paragraphs.en: A small playful suggestion may make an ordinary activity more enjoyable when everyone welcomes it. Whether that happens depends on timing and the people involved. The result does not establish social skill, resilience or the ability to make a group comfortable.
paragraphs.zh: 大家都欢迎时，一点玩乐提议可能让普通活动更有趣；是否如此，取决于时机与参与者。结果不能确定社交技巧、韧性或让集体舒服的能力。

paragraphs.en: Trying to lighten every moment can leave less room for disappointment or disagreement. Notice whether you are enjoying the exchange or feeling responsible for everyone’s mood. You can let a silence remain and still be a considerate participant.
paragraphs.zh: 如果每一刻都急着缓和，失望或分歧可能没机会说完。可以留意自己是在享受互动，还是觉得必须负责所有人的心情。让一段沉默留在那里，也可以是体贴的参与方式。

title.en: Humor, expression and atmosphere
title.zh: 幽默、表达与氛围

paragraphs.en: Surprised Commentator concerns expressing an immediate reaction to an unusual event. Lightener emphasizes looking for a playful element. Someone can react vividly without joking, or quietly enjoy a joke without retelling the event to anyone.
paragraphs.zh: “鲜活反应者”关注对意外事件马上表达反应；本主题更偏向寻找好玩的一面。一个人可以反应鲜明却不讲笑话，也可以安静享受玩笑而不向别人转述。

paragraphs.en: Atmosphere Seeker concerns choosing music, rituals or an easy gathering for the experience itself. Those choices do not require humor. Read the descriptions together when useful, but do not combine their counts into a sociability or happiness score.
paragraphs.zh: “氛围体验者”关注为了体验本身选择音乐、小仪式或轻松聚会，不一定需要幽默。可以一起读描述，但不要合成社交程度或幸福分数。

title.en: A small invitation with an easy exit
title.zh: 留有退出空间的小邀请

paragraphs.en: If you want an experiment, suggest one harmless addition to a routine activity: choosing a silly name for a shared shopping list, for example. Ask whether the other person wants to join in. A plain “not today” is enough to end the experiment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果想试一试，可以给日常活动提一个无害小点子，例如给共同购物清单取个好玩的名字。先问别人是否愿意参与；一句“今天不想”就足够结束尝试。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, recall the actual response rather than whether it matched your label. You may prefer a different tone next time. No exercise is necessary to complete the guide, and you do not need to laugh at yourself or reveal an embarrassing story.
paragraphs.zh: 之后回想真实回应，而不是有没有符合标签。下次你可以选择另一种语气。不做练习也能读完指南，更不必拿自己开玩笑或公开出糗经历。

title.en: A source theme, not a cheerfulness test
title.zh: 来源主题，不是快乐测验

The raw count is neither a norm nor a complete comparison of all twenty-five themes; every highest tie remains visible.
paragraphs.zh: Web修订版以自有HHHH主题为脉络，新写四条描述。每个主题出现四次，A、B各两次，面对不同对象。原始次数不是常模，也不是二十五主题的完整比较；全部最高并列都会保留。

paragraphs.en: All complete guides are freely available without answering. Public explanation links contain no personal count or answers. Feeling serious, sad or uninterested in this theme is not a failed result, and this game cannot assess your mental health.
paragraphs.zh: 不作答也能免费读全部完整指南。公开解释链接没有个人次数或答案。严肃、难过或对本主题没兴趣，都不是失败结果；游戏不能评估心理健康。

title.en: Making an expression feel like yours
title.zh: 让表达带一点自己的样子

paragraphs.en: Expressive Styler concerns choosing colors, details, a voice or a visual presentation that feels personally recognizable. The four descriptions ask about enjoying expression. They do not assess appearance, attractiveness, creativity, gender expression or how other people judge your style.
paragraphs.zh: “表达造型者”关注选择颜色、细节、语气或视觉呈现，让表达带一点自己的辨识度。四条描述问的是表达中的乐趣，不评外貌、吸引力、创造力、性别表达或别人怎样评价造型。

paragraphs.en: This may appear in a message, a notebook or an outfit chosen for an event you want to attend. You can care about one medium and have little interest in another. No particular clothing, spending level or public performance is required to recognize the theme.
paragraphs.zh: 它可以出现在一条消息、一本笔记或为自愿参加的活动准备的衣服里。你可以重视一种媒介，对另一种毫无兴趣；认得主题不需要特定穿着、花费或公开表演。

title.en: A small invitation with a personal detail
title.zh: 邀请里放一点个人细节

paragraphs.en: You invite friends to a meal and enjoy choosing a small drawing or a characteristic phrase for the message. The detail helps the invitation feel yours. Whether the meal is pleasant still depends on practical arrangements and the people attending, not on the design alone.
paragraphs.zh: 邀请朋友吃饭时，你喜欢给消息选一个小图案或一句带个人味道的话。细节让邀请更像自己；饭局是否愉快，仍取决于实际安排与参与者，不由设计单独决定。

paragraphs.en: A clear, plain message can serve the same purpose. Someone who spends no time on styling may care deeply about the gathering. The contrast in the questionnaire is about what feels more familiar to you, never which person makes a better friend.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚朴素的消息也能达到目的。完全不做造型的人，也可能十分在乎聚会。题中比较的是哪种描述更熟悉，不是谁更适合当朋友。

title.en: Enjoy the detail without an obligation to impress
title.zh: 享受细节，不必负责惊艳

paragraphs.en: A chosen detail may give you pleasure or communicate something you want to show. The count cannot establish originality or audience impact. A style can be meaningful to you even when nobody notices it, and a familiar style is not less legitimate than an unusual one.
paragraphs.zh: 选中的细节可能让你开心，或传达想表达的东西。次数不能证明原创程度或观众效果。即使无人注意，它也可以对你有意义；常见风格不比少见风格低一等。

paragraphs.en: Preparation can become tiring when every message or appearance feels like a test. Consider which details you enjoy and which you feel pressured to maintain. You may simplify, repeat an outfit or leave something unfinished without contradicting a supposed identity.
paragraphs.zh: 每条消息或每次露面都像考试时，准备会变累。可以分清哪些细节自己喜欢，哪些是觉得必须维持。简化、重复穿着或暂留未完成，都不违背什么固定身份。

title.en: Distinctive expression is not the same as attention
title.zh: 鲜明表达不等于需要关注

paragraphs.en: Surprised Commentator emphasizes how quickly a reaction becomes visible or verbal. Expressive Styler emphasizes shaping presentation. A quiet person may spend time on a distinctive visual detail; an animated speaker may prefer a completely plain presentation.
paragraphs.zh: “鲜活反应者”偏向反应多快变得可见或说出口；本主题偏向整理呈现方式。安静的人可能精心选择视觉细节，生动健谈的人也可能喜欢完全朴素的呈现。

paragraphs.en: Social Adapter emphasizes adjusting communication to different situations. Styling may stay consistent across situations, change for fun, or overlap with that adjustment. The separate counts cannot determine authenticity, confidence or a need for admiration.
paragraphs.zh: “场景切换者”偏向根据情境调整沟通。造型可以跨情境保持一致，也可以为了乐趣变化，或与这种调整重叠。独立次数不能确定真实程度、自信或被赞赏的需要。

title.en: Keep one detail for your own enjoyment
title.zh: 留一个自己喜欢的细节

paragraphs.en: If useful, choose one low-cost detail in an ordinary activity: a color in a personal note or a phrase in a message. Ask what you like about it before considering anyone else’s reaction. You can keep the activity private and need not buy or post anything.
paragraphs.zh: 如果觉得有用，可以在普通小事中选一个无需额外花费的细节，例如私人笔记的颜色或消息里一句话。先问自己喜欢什么，再考虑他人反应。可以完全私下完成，无需购买或发布。

paragraphs.en: Also notice whether making the detail took more time or energy than you wanted. Decide what would count as enough next time. Leaving a detail out is a valid choice, not evidence that you have lost creativity or personal identity.
paragraphs.zh: 也可以注意它是否花了比预想更多的时间或精力，想好下次做到哪里就够。不加细节也是有效选择，不表示失去创造力或个人身份。

title.en: A revised presentation of the source theme
title.zh: 来源主题的修订表达

paragraphs.en: The owned source code SEXY supplies editorial lineage only. This edition deliberately uses a presentation theme rather than an attractiveness judgment. Four new descriptions receive one point when selected; equal appearances do not make the scheduled comparisons a validated personality scale.
paragraphs.zh: 自有来源代码SEXY只保留编辑脉络。本版采用表达主题，不评价吸引力。新写四条描述被选中各记一次；出现次数相等，也不能把固定比较变成经过验证的人格量表。

paragraphs.en: Read every guide for free, including themes with no selections. A public guide or image contains general text, not your appearance or responses. These choices cannot decide clothing requirements, professional suitability or what anyone owes you.
paragraphs.zh: 包括零次主题在内，全部指南均可免费读。公开指南或图片只有通用文字，没有个人外貌或回答。这些选择不能决定穿着要求、职业适合度或他人对你的义务。

title.en: Easygoing: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 随和者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Easygoing concerns accepting several ordinary options, letting another person choose when your preference is minor, and saving attention on small comparisons. It does not establish passivity, agreeableness or emotional stability. Your answer describes a comparison in this game, not your response to every disagreement.
summary.zh: “随和者”关注接受几个日常选项、小偏好不重要时让别人选，以及不在细小比较上投入太多注意力。不确定被动、宜人性或情绪稳定程度；回答只是本次游戏的比较，不概括每场分歧。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.zh: 随和者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南
