description.zh: 免费完整阅读“随和者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Leaving minor choices open
title.zh: 让小选择保持余地

paragraphs.en: Easygoing concerns accepting several ordinary options, letting another person choose when your preference is minor, and saving attention on small comparisons. It does not establish passivity, agreeableness or emotional stability. Your answer describes a comparison in this game, not your response to every disagreement.
paragraphs.zh: “随和者”关注接受几个日常选项、小偏好不重要时让别人选，以及不在细小比较上投入太多注意力。不确定被动、宜人性或情绪稳定程度；回答只是本次游戏的比较，不概括每场分歧。

paragraphs.en: You can be flexible about lunch and firm about consent, pay or a commitment. Recognizing a low-stakes preference does not require accepting a serious change. The theme is most useful when you keep the words “minor” and “acceptable” in view.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以对午餐灵活，对同意、报酬或承诺坚定。认得低风险的小偏好，不要求接受重大改变。阅读时保留“不重要”与“可接受”这两个前提最有用。

title.en: Two cafés that both work
title.zh: 两家都可以的咖啡馆

paragraphs.en: A friend suggests two nearby cafés. Both fit your budget and access needs, and you genuinely have no strong preference. Letting the friend choose can be a complete decision. You need not invent a stronger preference to appear engaged.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友提出附近两家咖啡馆，都符合你的预算和出入需要，你也确实没有强烈偏好。让朋友选，可以是完整决定；不必为了显得投入，刻意制造一个更强烈的偏好。

paragraphs.en: If one café is inaccessible, too expensive or uncomfortable for you, the choice is no longer neutral. Saying so gives the other person useful information. Going along despite an important unmet need is a different situation from the low-stakes descriptions here.
paragraphs.zh: 如果一家出入不便、太贵或让你不舒服，选择就不再中性。说出来能给对方有用信息。重要需求未被满足却仍勉强顺从，与本页描述的低风险随和是不同情境。

title.en: Save attention and keep your preferences visible
title.zh: 省下注意力，也保留偏好

paragraphs.en: Choosing an acceptable option without searching for a perfect one may suit some everyday situations. The count does not measure decision quality or prove that this approach saves time. Practical constraints still matter, even when you feel relaxed about the choice.
paragraphs.zh: 日常有些情境适合选一个能接受的方案，不继续寻找完美选项。次数不测决定质量，也不证明这样一定节省时间；即使态度轻松，实际限制仍然重要。

paragraphs.en: If “anything is fine” becomes your automatic response, others may not know when something matters. You can say, “Either time works, but I do need to leave by six.” Flexibility and an explicit limit can coexist without becoming opposite personality types.
paragraphs.zh: 如果“都行”成了自动回答，别人可能不知道什么对你重要。可以说“两个时间都可以，但我六点前需要离开”。灵活与明确限制可以并存，无需归为相反人格。

title.en: Flexibility, improvising and quiet priorities
title.zh: 随和、应变与安静的取舍

paragraphs.en: Improviser concerns finding a workable replacement when circumstances remove part of a plan. Easygoing concerns being comfortable with acceptable variation. You can tolerate a change without wanting to design an alternative, or improvise carefully around a strong preference.
paragraphs.zh: “灵活应对者”关注条件变化后找替代方案；本主题关注能否舒服地接受可接受的变化。你可以接受改变却不想设计替代，也可以带着强烈偏好认真应变。

paragraphs.en: Quiet Observer concerns leaving some achievement or comparison goals aside. That is broader than letting someone select a minor option. Neither theme measures indifference or virtue, and their counts should not be merged into a detachment score.
paragraphs.zh: “静观者”关注放下一部分成就或比较目标，比把小选项交给别人更广。两个主题都不衡量冷漠或品德，也不应合成抽离程度分数。

title.en: Say what is flexible and what is fixed
title.zh: 分别说清可变与固定部分

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary plan, identify an acceptable range before replying. You might name two workable times and one real limit. Then let the other person choose within that range. This is an optional communication experiment, not an instruction to become more accommodating.
paragraphs.zh: 面对一项普通安排，可以先找出能接受的范围再回复。例如给出两个可行时间，再说明一个真实限制，让对方在范围内选。这只是可选沟通尝试，不要求变得更加迁就。

paragraphs.en: After the plan, notice whether you were comfortable or had left something important unsaid. Either observation is more specific than a label. You may revise your preference later when new information appears; a game result is not a promise to keep agreeing.
paragraphs.zh: 安排后，留意自己是否舒服，或有没有漏说重要事情。两种观察都比标签具体。出现新信息时可以修改偏好；游戏结果不是必须一直同意的承诺。

title.en: Four choices do not define your boundaries
title.zh: 四次选择不能定义边界

paragraphs.en: OJBK is the owned source theme behind this revised reading. Its four new descriptions each appear once, with two A and two B positions. The count is out of four scheduled comparisons, not a population percentile or a complete ordering of all themes.
paragraphs.zh: OJBK是修订读法背后的自有来源主题。新写四条描述各出现一次，A、B位置各两次。次数来自四个固定比较，不是人口百分位，也不是所有主题的完整排序。

paragraphs.en: All highest ties remain valid, and every complete guide is free without a personal result. Public links contain general descriptions only. No score overrides your right to refuse, change your mind or explain what an arrangement requires.
paragraphs.zh: 最高并列都有效，没有个人结果也能免费读全部指南。公开链接只有通用描述。任何次数都不取消拒绝、改变想法或说明安排条件的权利。

title.en: Resource Keeper: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 资源守护者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Resource Keeper names choices about checking time, money and energy before adding another commitment. The descriptions concern managing a limited allowance in a particular situation. They do not measure financial literacy, wealth, poverty, generosity or your ability to provide for others.
summary.zh: “资源守护者”指新增承诺前，核对时间、金钱与精力的选择。描述关注具体情境下怎样安排有限余地，不衡量理财知识、贫富、慷慨程度或供养他人的能力。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Resource Keeper | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 资源守护者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Resource Keeper theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“资源守护者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Checking what an agreement will cost
title.zh: 先核对答应之后要付出什么

paragraphs.en: Resource Keeper names choices about checking time, money and energy before adding another commitment. The descriptions concern managing a limited allowance in a particular situation. They do not measure financial literacy, wealth, poverty, generosity or your ability to provide for others.
paragraphs.zh: “资源守护者”指新增承诺前，核对时间、金钱与精力的选择。描述关注具体情境下怎样安排有限余地，不衡量理财知识、贫富、慷慨程度或供养他人的能力。

paragraphs.en: You may protect time carefully while spending freely on one valued hobby. Another person may have little room to choose at all. A larger count cannot distinguish a preference from necessity, so keep your actual circumstances beside the reading.
paragraphs.zh: 你可能谨慎保护时间，却愿意为重视的兴趣花钱；另一个人可能根本没有多少选择余地。较多次数不能区分偏好与不得已，请把实际处境一起保留。

title.en: A worthwhile invitation with a continuing cost
title.zh: 不错的邀请，也有后续成本

paragraphs.en: A weekly class looks enjoyable, but attendance would also require travel and preparation. You check the whole commitment rather than the first session alone. You might choose a shorter course, decline for now or decide the continuing cost is acceptable.
paragraphs.zh: 每周课程很有趣，但参加还需要通勤与准备。你核对的是整个承诺，不只第一节课。之后可能选更短的课程、暂时不参加，或决定持续成本可以接受。

paragraphs.en: None of those outcomes follows from the theme label. A person can review resources carefully and still choose an expensive experience. Likewise, declining can reflect a hard constraint rather than a stable preference for caution.
paragraphs.zh: 这些结果都不是标签规定的。认真核对资源后，也可以选择花费较大的体验；拒绝也可能来自硬性限制，而不是稳定的谨慎偏好。

title.en: Protect room without judging every pleasure
title.zh: 保留余地，不必审判每份乐趣

paragraphs.en: Checking continuing demands can make a hidden tradeoff visible. Whether it helps depends on the information available and what matters to you. The questionnaire cannot determine an affordable amount, a correct budget or whether a purchase is worthwhile.
paragraphs.zh: 核对持续要求，可以让隐含的取舍变得可见。是否有帮助，取决于掌握的信息与个人重视的东西。问卷不能决定负担得起的数额、正确预算或消费是否值得。

paragraphs.en: Repeatedly reviewing a small expense may itself use attention. Notice whether you need another fact or simply permission to choose within your own limits. Enjoyment is a legitimate consideration; the theme is not a moral ranking of saving over spending.
paragraphs.zh: 反复核对一笔小开销，本身也会占用注意力。可以留意自己是缺一条信息，还是需要允许自己在限度内作决定。乐趣也是合理考虑；本主题不把节省排在花费之上作道德评价。

title.en: Resources, risks and contributions
title.zh: 资源、风险与投入

paragraphs.en: Risk Watcher emphasizes uncertain information and possible obstacles. Resource Keeper emphasizes what a commitment would consume even when everything goes as expected. A perfectly predictable plan can still require more time than you want to offer.
paragraphs.zh: “预警者”关注不确定信息与可能障碍；本主题关注即使一切如期，承诺仍会消耗什么。完全可预测的计划，也可能需要超过你愿意提供的时间。

paragraphs.en: Giver emphasizes personally contributing to someone or a shared activity. Protecting resources does not mean caring less. You can offer help after checking your capacity, and you can care about someone without being able to provide what they need.
paragraphs.zh: “投入付出者”关注向别人或共同活动具体投入。保护资源不表示更少在乎。核对能力范围后仍可帮忙；即使无法提供所需，也可以关心一个人。

title.en: Name one limit before answering
title.zh: 回复之前先说清一个限度

paragraphs.en: For an ordinary optional plan, list its immediate demand and one continuing demand. Choose a limit that belongs to you, such as one evening or a fixed amount of preparation. You need not disclose financial or personal details to anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 面对一项可选普通安排，写下即时要求与一项后续要求，再给自己定一个限度，例如一个晚上或固定准备时长。不必向任何人披露财务或私人细节。

paragraphs.en: Use the limit to form a concrete reply: “I can help for this hour, but not take the whole task.” Review the actual outcome later. This exercise is optional and provides no financial, employment or care-management advice.
paragraphs.zh: 可以据此作具体回复：“我能帮这一个小时，但不能接下整件事。”之后再看实际结果。练习可以不做，也不提供财务、就业或照护管理建议。

title.en: A safe theme name with a narrow meaning
title.zh: 安全名称与有限含义

paragraphs.en: The owned source code POOR is retained only as a provenance identifier. This Web reading makes no inference about poverty. Four new literal descriptions contribute zero to four selections, with equal A/B appearances but different scheduled opponents. The count is not a norm or a full ranking of priorities.
paragraphs.zh: 自有来源代码POOR只作为溯源标识保留，Web读法不推断贫困。新写四条字面描述产生零到四次选择，A/B出现均等，但比较对象不同。次数不是常模，也不是优先事项的完整排名。

paragraphs.en: All guides can be read without answering, and public links contain no personal resources or responses. Actual decisions need your circumstances and, when appropriate, relevant qualified advice. A playful label cannot establish what you can afford or owe.
paragraphs.zh: 全部指南无需作答即可阅读，公开链接没有个人资源状况或回答。真实决定需要结合处境，必要时参考相应专业建议。趣味标签不能确定负担能力或义务。

title.en: Risk Watcher: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 预警者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Risk Watcher concerns asking what could prevent a plan from working, checking an uncertain detail and raising a possible problem early. These are self-described choices. They do not measure actual risk, anxiety, pessimism, foresight or the accuracy of your predictions.
summary.zh: “预警者”关注追问计划可能在哪儿受阻、核对不确定细节，以及较早提出可能问题。这是自述选择，不测实际风险、焦虑、悲观、远见或预测准确度。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Risk Watcher | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 预警者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Risk Watcher theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“预警者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Noticing what has not yet been checked
title.zh: 注意还没核实的地方

paragraphs.en: Risk Watcher concerns asking what could prevent a plan from working, checking an uncertain detail and raising a possible problem early. These are self-described choices. They do not measure actual risk, anxiety, pessimism, foresight or the accuracy of your predictions.
paragraphs.zh: “预警者”关注追问计划可能在哪儿受阻、核对不确定细节，以及较早提出可能问题。这是自述选择，不测实际风险、焦虑、悲观、远见或预测准确度。

paragraphs.en: One context can invite careful checking while another feels familiar enough to proceed. A count cannot tell whether a concern was justified or how often you notice problems outside these four comparisons. A concrete example is more informative than an identity label.
paragraphs.zh: 某个情境适合仔细核对，另一个则熟悉到可以直接前进。次数不能确定担忧是否有依据，也不能判断这四个比较之外多常注意问题。具体例子比身份标签更有信息。

title.en: A date that looks confirmed
title.zh: 看起来已经确定的日期

paragraphs.en: A group is excited about an event and starts arranging transport. You notice that the date came from an old message and ask someone to confirm it. The useful part is the checkable question: which date is current and where can it be verified?
paragraphs.zh: 大家兴奋地准备活动，开始安排交通。你注意到日期来自旧消息，便请人确认。有用之处是可核实的问题：现在到底是哪天，能到哪里查证？

paragraphs.en: The date may turn out to be correct. Raising a concern does not make it a prediction that must come true. Nor does one correct concern prove that every worry deserves the same response; the evidence and practical consequence still need attention.
paragraphs.zh: 日期也可能本来就正确。提出疑问不等于作出了必须应验的预测；一次疑问正确，也不证明每份担心都应得到相同回应，仍需看证据与实际后果。

title.en: Turn a concern into a bounded check
title.zh: 把担忧变成有限核对

paragraphs.en: An early question may uncover a missing dependency before people commit. It can also interrupt momentum when the concern is too vague to investigate. The game cannot decide which happened; notice whether you identified a specific uncertainty and a proportionate way to check it.
paragraphs.zh: 早一点的问题可能在投入前发现遗漏条件；太模糊、无从调查的担忧也可能打断进展。游戏不能判定是哪种情况，可以看自己是否指出具体未知，以及相称的核对办法。

paragraphs.en: Some uncertainty remains after reasonable checking. You do not need certainty about everything to make an ordinary decision. If a concern persists, distinguish what you can verify, what someone else owns and what you can simply leave unresolved.
paragraphs.zh: 合理核对后仍会有不确定性。普通决定不要求先对一切确定。担忧持续时，可以区分自己能查什么、什么由别人负责，以及什么可以暂时不解决。

title.en: Identifying an issue and preparing a fallback
title.zh: 发现问题与准备替代

paragraphs.en: Contingency Planner emphasizes organizing next steps and fallback arrangements. Risk Watcher emphasizes finding a possible weak point or questioning the information first. You can notice an obstacle without wanting to coordinate its solution.
paragraphs.zh: “预案者”偏向组织步骤与替代安排；本主题偏向先注意薄弱处或追问信息。发现障碍，不表示一定想负责协调解决。

paragraphs.en: Reflective Thinker considers alternative explanations and connections within a problem. That inquiry may have nothing to do with a negative outcome. Keep the themes separate rather than treating every careful thought as caution or every caution as overthinking.
paragraphs.zh: “反复思考者”考虑解释与问题内部的联系，未必涉及负面后果。可以分别理解，不把每次仔细思考都叫谨慎，也不把每次谨慎都叫想太多。

title.en: One question, one source, one stopping point
title.zh: 一个问题、一个来源、一个停止点

paragraphs.en: For a low-stakes plan, write one concern as a question with an observable answer. Identify a suitable source and decide what would count as enough information. If no answer is available, name the remaining uncertainty without presenting it as a fact.
paragraphs.zh: 对低风险计划，把一份担忧写成能观察答案的问题，找一个合适来源，再决定查到什么程度就够。没有答案时，明确说仍未知，不把未知当成事实。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, notice whether the check changed the plan or merely reassured you temporarily. Either observation can guide a later choice. You need not repeat the exercise, and it is not a treatment for persistent worry or a substitute for safety procedures.
paragraphs.zh: 之后注意核对是否改变了计划，还是仅暂时安心。两种观察都可供下次参考。不必反复练习；它不治疗持续担忧，也不代替安全规程。

title.en: An editorial warning theme, not a risk score
title.zh: 编辑主题，不是风险分数

paragraphs.en: OH-NO is the owned source theme behind these four new descriptions. Each appears once in the fifty comparisons. Every theme has two A and two B positions, but faces different opponents; a zero-to-four count is not a validated caution trait or an ordering of all twenty-five themes.
paragraphs.zh: OH-NO是四条新描述背后的自有来源主题，各在五十组比较中出现一次。每个主题A、B各两次，但对手不同；零到四次不代表经过验证的谨慎特质，也不排序全部二十五主题。

paragraphs.en: Every full guide is free, including themes you did not select. Public links contain no concerns or personal responses. For real health, legal, financial or safety decisions, the relevant facts and procedures matter; this result cannot certify a choice as safe.
paragraphs.zh: 全部完整指南免费，包括未选主题。公开链接不包含个人担忧或回答。真实健康、法律、财务或安全决定应依据相关事实与规程；本结果不能认证选择安全。

title.en: Quiet Observer: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 静观者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Quiet Observer concerns enjoying a quiet activity, leaving some comparisons aside and valuing time without a visible achievement. It describes what you might choose in certain ordinary moments. It does not assess spiritual attainment, ambition, religion or emotional detachment.
summary.zh: “静观者”关注享受安静活动、放下一部分比较，以及看重不必交成果的时间。它描述某些日常时刻可能的选择，不评精神境界、抱负、宗教或情感疏离。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Quiet Observer | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 静观者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Quiet Observer theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“静观者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Letting an ordinary moment be sufficient
title.zh: 让普通时刻也可以足够

paragraphs.en: Quiet Observer concerns enjoying a quiet activity, leaving some comparisons aside and valuing time without a visible achievement. It describes what you might choose in certain ordinary moments. It does not assess spiritual attainment, ambition, religion or emotional detachment.
paragraphs.zh: “静观者”关注享受安静活动、放下一部分比较，以及看重不必交成果的时间。它描述某些日常时刻可能的选择，不评精神境界、抱负、宗教或情感疏离。

paragraphs.en: You can want a peaceful evening and still pursue an important long-term goal. You can also enjoy a large event without needing it to confer status. The theme is not an instruction to withdraw from activities, relationships or responsibilities you value.
paragraphs.zh: 想要平静夜晚，也可以追求重要长期目标；享受盛大活动，也不一定为了地位。主题不要求退出自己重视的活动、关系或职责。

title.en: An interest that stays an interest
title.zh: 兴趣可以先只是兴趣

paragraphs.en: You enjoy drawing in a notebook. When someone suggests posting daily and building an audience, you decide to keep it private for now. The activity can remain worthwhile to you without a following, a target or a visible improvement record.
paragraphs.zh: 你喜欢在本子上画画。有人建议每天发布、经营观众时，你决定暂时私下画。没有粉丝、目标或可展示的进步记录，这项活动也可以对你有意义。

paragraphs.en: Another day you might choose a class or a public exhibition. That would not invalidate the earlier choice. A quiet activity is not inherently more authentic, and wanting recognition is not automatically a problem; the relevant question is what you want from this particular activity.
paragraphs.zh: 另一天也可能选择上课或参加公开展览，不会使此前选择失效。安静活动不天然更真实，想被认可也不自动成问题。关键是自己希望从这项具体活动得到什么。

title.en: Enough can be a choice, not a verdict
title.zh: 足够是一种选择，不是裁决

paragraphs.en: Leaving an optional comparison aside may make room for an experience you enjoy. Whether that helps depends on the situation. The count does not prove contentment, wisdom or a lower need for connection, and it cannot distinguish a chosen pause from a lack of opportunity.
paragraphs.zh: 放下一场可选比较，可能给喜欢的体验留出空间；是否有帮助取决于情境。次数不能证明满足、智慧或较少的连接需要，也不能区分自愿停顿与缺少机会。

paragraphs.en: A wish for quiet can also leave something important unsaid if you use it to avoid every necessary conversation. You can prefer a peaceful pace while making a request or addressing an obligation. No label decides which commitments should stay.
paragraphs.zh: 如果用安静避开所有必要交谈，也可能让重要事情没被说出。偏好平和节奏，仍可以提出请求或面对义务。标签不能决定哪些承诺应保留。

title.en: Quiet priorities and temporary distance
title.zh: 安静取舍与暂时拉开距离

paragraphs.en: Detached Observer concerns stepping back from a noisy interaction to decide whether to engage. Quiet Observer concerns whether a larger occasion or visible achievement is wanted in the first place. Enjoying a quiet hobby does not establish disengagement from people.
paragraphs.zh: “抽离观察者”偏向从嘈杂互动中退一步，再决定是否参与；本主题偏向原本是否想要更大场面或可见成果。喜欢安静兴趣，不表示疏离他人。

paragraphs.en: Pause Taker concerns inserting a break or a gap between demands. You might pause in order to return to a busy project, while valuing unproductive time for its own sake is a different choice. Neither count measures energy, depression or a preferred permanent lifestyle.
paragraphs.zh: “休眠者”关注在要求之间加一段间歇。暂停可能是为了回到忙碌项目；看重没有产出的时间本身，是另一种选择。两项都不测精力、抑郁或永久生活方式。

title.en: Ask what you want the activity to do
title.zh: 问问希望活动承载什么

paragraphs.en: Choose one ordinary interest and finish the sentence, “For now, I want this to give me…” You might name enjoyment, practice, company or recognition. More than one answer can fit. There is no requirement to choose the quietest or least ambitious option.
paragraphs.zh: 选一项普通兴趣，补完“目前，我希望它带来……”：可以是乐趣、练习、陪伴或认可，多个答案也可以并存。无需选最安静或最不显抱负的答案。

paragraphs.en: If a small change would make it easier to enjoy, try that change once and review the experience. You may leave the activity as it is. The reflection needs no public declaration and does not ask you to give up an important goal.
paragraphs.zh: 若一个小调整能让体验更舒服，可以只试一次再回顾；也可以维持现状。反思不需要公开宣言，更不要求放弃重要目标。

title.en: No religious or health classification
title.zh: 不作宗教或健康归类

paragraphs.en: The source code MONK identifies the owned editorial theme, not a religious affiliation. This repair replaces broad character claims with four concrete descriptions. Equal exposure means four comparisons per theme, not complete pairwise measurement or a population norm.
paragraphs.zh: 来源代码MONK标记自有编辑主题，不表示宗教归属。修订版用四条具体描述替代宽泛人物评价。均等出现表示每主题四次比较，不是完整两两测量或人口常模。

paragraphs.en: The raw choices and all highest ties can be read alongside any free full guide. Public explanation pages contain no personal answers. If a change in activity or interest is causing concern, this entertainment label cannot explain its cause or replace appropriate support.
paragraphs.zh: 原始选择与全部最高并列，可以结合任一免费指南阅读。公开解释页没有个人回答。若活动或兴趣变化让你担心，娱乐标签不能解释原因，也不能代替合适支持。

title.en: Venting Fixer: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 吐槽补位者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Venting Fixer concerns voicing frustration while helping with a defined part of a problem. Its descriptions allow irritation and action to coexist. The count does not measure reliability, sacrifice, anger control or how often you rescue a group.
summary.zh: “吐槽补位者”关注一边说出不满，一边帮忙处理问题中的明确部分。描述允许烦躁与行动并存，次数不测可靠性、牺牲程度、愤怒控制或替集体救场的频率。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Venting Fixer | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 吐槽补位者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Venting Fixer theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“吐槽补位者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Expressing irritation while taking a practical part
title.zh: 说出不满，也接住具体一块

paragraphs.en: Venting Fixer concerns voicing frustration while helping with a defined part of a problem. Its descriptions allow irritation and action to coexist. The count does not measure reliability, sacrifice, anger control or how often you rescue a group.
paragraphs.zh: “吐槽补位者”关注一边说出不满，一边帮忙处理问题中的明确部分。描述允许烦躁与行动并存，次数不测可靠性、牺牲程度、愤怒控制或替集体救场的频率。

paragraphs.en: You may recognize it in a shared household task but choose not to help with another request. The theme cannot establish that you secretly enjoy carrying extra work. Agreeing to one part also does not imply agreement to the whole situation.
paragraphs.zh: 你可能在共同家务中认得它，却拒绝另一项请求。主题不能证明其实喜欢多承担；答应其中一部分，也不代表赞同整个安排。

title.en: A confusing shared list
title.zh: 一份混乱的共同清单

paragraphs.en: A group’s shopping list contains duplicates. You say that the repeated confusion is frustrating and offer to check one category this time. The offer names a task; the complaint names a problem. Neither needs to erase the other.
paragraphs.zh: 共同购物清单出现重复，你说反复混乱很让人烦，并提出这次核对一个类别。提议说明任务，不满说明问题，二者无需互相抵消。

paragraphs.en: If you quietly check every category after agreeing to only one, others may not see the extra effort or know what needs changing. A practical correction can be useful without creating a standing obligation to fix the same problem every time.
paragraphs.zh: 如果只答应一个类别，却默默核对全部，别人可能看不见额外投入，也不知道哪里需要改变。一次实际补救可以有用，但不会自动形成以后每次都要补位的义务。

title.en: Helping does not cancel a complaint
title.zh: 帮忙不取消提出问题的资格

paragraphs.en: Naming a problem while contributing may make both your concern and your available help clearer. That is a possible outcome, not a skill proven by the result. Timing, wording and the other people’s willingness to respond all affect what happens.
paragraphs.zh: 一边提出问题一边投入，可能让关切与可提供的帮助都更清楚。这只是可能结果，不是测验已证明的技能；时机、措辞和别人是否愿意回应都会影响结果。

paragraphs.en: Repeated venting without a specific request may leave others unsure what to do. Repeated helping without a limit may leave you overcommitted. Consider whether you want acknowledgment, a change in the arrangement, a smaller role or simply room to stop.
paragraphs.zh: 反复吐槽却没有具体请求，可能让别人不知道怎样回应；反复帮忙却不设限，可能使自己承担过多。可以分清需要的是被听见、改变安排、缩小职责，还是停止的余地。

title.en: Speaking pressure and organizing a repair
title.zh: 表达压力与组织补救

paragraphs.en: Pressure Speaker concerns stating strain, a limit or a need to renegotiate. It does not require taking on the repair. Venting Fixer includes choosing a practical contribution alongside the irritation. Saying “I cannot take this on” remains a complete response.
paragraphs.zh: “直抒压力者”关注说明压力、限度或重新协商需要，不要求接下补救。本主题包含带着不满选择一项具体投入。“我接不下这件事”仍是完整回应。

paragraphs.en: Initiator concerns offering a shared starting point or tracking an agreed next step. You can organize calmly without venting, or help with one narrow part without coordinating the group. The separate themes do not form a competence hierarchy.
paragraphs.zh: “带队推进者”关注提出共同起点、跟进商定步骤。可以平静组织而不吐槽，也可以只帮窄小一块、不协调集体。几个主题不组成能力等级。

title.en: Separate the problem from your offer
title.zh: 把问题与自己的提议分开

paragraphs.en: If appropriate, use two sentences for an ordinary issue: “The repeated changes are wearing me down. I can update this page once, but we need someone to confirm the final details.” Name what you can offer and what requires another agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 合适时，可以用两句话处理普通问题：“反复改动让我很累。这页我可以再更新一次，但最终细节需要有人确认。”分别说清能提供什么，以及什么还需要另行商定。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, check whether the limit was understood and whether you still want the role. You do not need to prove helpfulness by accepting more. The exercise is optional and is not a reason to stay in an unsafe or unfair arrangement.
paragraphs.zh: 之后核对限度是否被理解、自己是否仍愿意承担。不必靠继续多接来证明愿意帮忙。练习可不做，也不是留在不安全或不公平安排中的理由。

title.en: A bounded repair of the source theme
title.zh: 来源主题的有限修订

paragraphs.en: SHIT is retained as the owned source identifier, not as a judgment of anyone. This edition uses four new descriptions about frustration and a defined contribution. Their zero-to-four count is not a norm, duty score or complete comparison with all other themes; all highest ties are retained.
paragraphs.zh: SHIT仅保留为自有来源标识，不评价任何人。本版新写四条关于不满与明确投入的描述。零到四次不是常模、责任程度或与全部主题的完整比较；所有最高并列都保留。

paragraphs.en: Every guide is free before answering, and public links contain no personal complaint, score or answer sheet. Real working agreements depend on roles and consent. A game result cannot assign you responsibility for somebody else’s unfinished task.
paragraphs.zh: 作答前也能免费读全部指南，公开链接没有私人不满、次数或答卷。真实分工取决于职责与同意；游戏结果不能把别人的未完成工作分给你。

title.en: Appreciator: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 记好者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Appreciator concerns remembering an ordinary kindness, acknowledging what helped and hearing an explanation before deciding what a mistake means. These descriptions offer a way to reflect on particular responses. They do not measure kindness, forgiveness, trustworthiness or moral worth.
summary.zh: “记好者”关注记住日常善意、说明什么有帮助，以及判断失误意义前先听解释。描述供反思具体回应，不测善良、宽容、可信程度或道德价值。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Appreciator | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 记好者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Appreciator theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“记好者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Remembering a helpful detail
title.zh: 记住一项具体帮助

paragraphs.en: Appreciator concerns remembering an ordinary kindness, acknowledging what helped and hearing an explanation before deciding what a mistake means. These descriptions offer a way to reflect on particular responses. They do not measure kindness, forgiveness, trustworthiness or moral worth.
paragraphs.zh: “记好者”关注记住日常善意、说明什么有帮助，以及判断失误意义前先听解释。描述供反思具体回应，不测善良、宽容、可信程度或道德价值。

paragraphs.en: You may be grateful for one action and still disagree with the same person. You may listen to an explanation and decide it does not resolve the problem. The theme never requires replacing evidence about harm with a positive interpretation.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以感谢一个行动，同时仍不同意同一个人；听过解释后，也可以认为问题尚未解决。主题从不要求用积极解释取代伤害的事实。

title.en: Saying what made a difficult day easier
title.zh: 说清哪件事让一天轻松一点

paragraphs.en: During a busy afternoon, someone brings a document you had left behind. Later you say, “That saved me a return trip; thank you.” The acknowledgment names an observable action and its effect on you without making a sweeping claim about the person.
paragraphs.zh: 忙碌下午，有人送来你落下的文件。之后你说：“这让我少跑了一趟，谢谢。”感谢指出可见行动及对自己的帮助，不必顺势给对方作全面评价。

paragraphs.en: The same person may also miss an agreed deadline. You can appreciate the document and discuss the deadline separately. One helpful act does not create a debt, require trust in unrelated situations or cancel a request for something to change.
paragraphs.zh: 同一个人也可能错过商定期限。可以感谢送文件，同时另谈期限。一项帮助不产生债务，不要求在无关事情上信任，也不取消提出改变的资格。

title.en: Specific appreciation leaves room for complexity
title.zh: 具体感谢容得下复杂情况

paragraphs.en: A concrete acknowledgment may help someone understand what you valued. The count cannot show whether your message was effective or how the other person felt. Silent appreciation, cultural conventions and limited opportunities can all affect whether you recognize these descriptions.
paragraphs.zh: 具体感谢可能让对方理解你看重什么。次数不能说明表达是否有效或对方感受。私下记得、文化习惯和机会有限，都可能影响是否认得这些描述。

paragraphs.en: Searching for something good in every situation can become pressure if it stops you naming disappointment. You do not owe a grateful interpretation of mistreatment. Appreciation is optional and can coexist with a boundary, an unresolved concern or a decision to leave.
paragraphs.zh: 如果因此无法说失望，凡事找好处也会变成压力。面对不当对待，不欠任何人感恩式解释。感谢是可选的，可以与边界、未解决的关切或离开的决定并存。

title.en: Acknowledging, caring and contributing
title.zh: 感谢、照应与投入

paragraphs.en: Caregiver focuses on noticing another person’s comfort and offering care. Appreciator focuses on recognizing something received or considering a specific explanation. You can value another person’s help without wanting a caregiving role.
paragraphs.zh: “照应者”关注留意别人的舒服程度、提供关心；本主题关注认出已收到的帮助，或考虑具体解释。珍惜别人的帮助，不表示想担任照护角色。

paragraphs.en: Giver focuses on offering time or resources. Acknowledging a gift is not a promise to return an equal contribution. The counts are separate observations and cannot produce a kindness balance, a relationship ledger or a ranking of good people.
paragraphs.zh: “投入付出者”关注提供时间或资源。感谢一份帮助，不是答应等额回报。几个次数分别观察，不能生成善良平衡、关系账目或好人排名。

title.en: A thank-you with no extra obligation
title.zh: 不附带额外义务的感谢

paragraphs.en: If you want to, identify one small action that helped and describe it plainly. You can thank the person, write a private note or do nothing further. Public praise, disclosure and contact are not necessary, particularly when a relationship feels uncomfortable.
paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，可以找一项确实有帮助的小行动，朴素描述。可以向对方感谢、写私人笔记，也可以不再行动。无需公开表扬、披露或联系，尤其在关系让人不舒服时。

paragraphs.en: Separately ask whether anything still needs discussion. Keeping these two observations apart can make the reflection clearer. You do not need to resolve a disagreement, forgive someone or feel a particular emotion to complete the guide.
paragraphs.zh: 另外再问，是否还有事需要讨论。把两种观察分开，能让反思更清楚。不必解决分歧、原谅谁或产生规定情绪，才能完成阅读。

title.en: No gratitude or forgiveness scale
title.zh: 不是感恩或宽容量表

paragraphs.en: The owned THAN-K theme provides editorial context for these four new descriptions. Each is offered once against a scheduled alternative, with two A and two B appearances overall. Counts reflect those choices, not a norm, stable disposition or a complete twenty-five-theme ranking.
paragraphs.zh: 自有THAN-K主题为四条新描述提供编辑脉络。每条只与固定另一项比较一次，整体A、B各出现两次。次数反映这些选择，不是常模、稳定性格或二十五主题的完整排名。

paragraphs.en: All full guides are public and free without answering. Explanation links contain no personal history or counts. If an interaction involves real harm or safety concerns, a positive theme label supplies neither evidence nor an obligation to remain involved.
paragraphs.zh: 不答题也能免费读全部公开指南。解释链接没有私人经历或次数。互动若涉及真实伤害或安全问题，积极主题标签既不能提供证据，也不要求继续参与。

title.en: Improviser: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 灵活应对者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Improviser concerns finding a detour, rearranging available resources and using a temporary workable arrangement when circumstances change. It records descriptions you chose, not an ability test. A count cannot show whether the alternative was successful, safe or efficient.
summary.zh: “灵活应对者”关注条件变化后找替代路、重排现有资源，以及暂用一个可行安排。它记录选中的描述，不是能力测试；次数不能说明替代方案是否成功、安全或高效。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Improviser | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 灵活应对者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Improviser theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“灵活应对者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Working with the pieces still available
title.zh: 用仍在手里的条件调整

paragraphs.en: Improviser concerns finding a detour, rearranging available resources and using a temporary workable arrangement when circumstances change. It records descriptions you chose, not an ability test. A count cannot show whether the alternative was successful, safe or efficient.
paragraphs.zh: “灵活应对者”关注条件变化后找替代路、重排现有资源，以及暂用一个可行安排。它记录选中的描述，不是能力测试；次数不能说明替代方案是否成功、安全或高效。

paragraphs.en: You may improvise comfortably in a hobby and prefer established procedures in a serious task. That difference is appropriate context. This theme does not ask you to ignore requirements, perform work outside your competence or make every disruption into an opportunity.
paragraphs.zh: 兴趣活动中可能愿意即兴，严肃任务中则偏好既定流程。这种差别是必要背景。主题不要求忽略条件、做超出能力的工作，或把每次中断都当机会。

title.en: A venue becomes unavailable
title.zh: 原定场地不能用了

paragraphs.en: A small voluntary gathering loses its planned room. You look at the remaining time, people and available spaces, then suggest a shorter outdoor meeting if everyone wants it. You are adapting the plan rather than proving that the original plan never mattered.
paragraphs.zh: 小型自愿聚会的原定房间不能用了。你看剩余时间、参与者与可用地点，提议大家愿意时改为短一些的户外见面。这是在调整计划，不是证明原计划毫无意义。

paragraphs.en: Accessibility, weather or a participant’s preference may make that alternative unsuitable. Cancelling or postponing can be the workable decision. A temporary workaround does not override another person’s needs or the requirements that made the original venue important.
paragraphs.zh: 出入条件、天气或参与者偏好，可能让替代不合适。取消或延期也可以是可行决定。临时方案不取消他人的需要，也不替代原场地之所以重要的条件。

title.en: A temporary fix needs a visible boundary
title.zh: 临时方案也要看得见边界

paragraphs.en: Rearranging what is available may preserve part of an activity when the first route closes. Whether it does is an outcome to inspect, not something the label guarantees. A modest alternative can be enough without pretending to reproduce everything originally planned.
paragraphs.zh: 重排现有条件，可能在原路不通时保住一部分活动；是否如此需要看结果，标签不保证。小一点的替代可以足够，无需假装完整复现最初计划。

paragraphs.en: A quick workaround can become confusing if nobody knows it is temporary. Name what it leaves out and when it should be reviewed. You can also stop adapting when each new patch creates more effort than the activity is worth to you.
paragraphs.zh: 临时办法若没说清暂时性，可能造成混乱。应说明缺什么、何时再看；如果每次补丁都让成本超过自己觉得值得的程度，也可以停止调整。

title.en: Starting, accepting and rearranging
title.zh: 开始、接受与重排

paragraphs.en: Action Starter concerns trying a small first part before the whole plan is settled. Improviser concerns rearranging after a condition changes. Someone can like early experiments but dislike interruptions, or prefer a full starting plan and adapt it later.
paragraphs.zh: “先行者”偏向计划尚未完整时先试小部分；本主题偏向条件改变后的重排。一个人可以喜欢早试却不喜欢打断，也可以先做完整计划、之后再调整。

paragraphs.en: Easygoing concerns being comfortable with acceptable variation, not creating a replacement. You can accept a changed plan while leaving its redesign to someone else. These counts do not rank adaptability, flexibility or problem-solving intelligence.
paragraphs.zh: “随和者”关注舒服地接受可接受变化，不一定设计替代。可以接受改动，把重新安排交给别人。次数不排名适应力、灵活性或解决问题的智力。

title.en: Name the smallest useful alternative
title.zh: 说清最小可用替代

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes disruption, identify what still matters and what can change. Suggest the smallest alternative that preserves that purpose, while naming any lost feature. Ask affected people rather than assuming they welcome the adaptation.
paragraphs.zh: 面对一次低风险中断，分清什么仍重要、什么能变。提出保住目的的最小替代，同时说清会失去什么，并问受影响的人，不假设大家欢迎调整。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, decide whether to keep, revise or discard it. There is no bonus for preserving a plan at all costs. This optional exercise does not replace professional procedures, safety checks or another person’s agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 之后决定保留、修改或放弃。无论代价都要保住计划，不会得到额外奖励。可选练习不替代专业规程、安全核对或他人同意。

title.en: A new literal reading of MALO
title.zh: MALO的字面修订读法

paragraphs.en: MALO identifies the owned source theme. Four original Web descriptions are each compared once, with two A and two B appearances per theme. Different opponents mean the raw zero-to-four counts cannot establish a complete ordering of the twenty-five themes or a validated adaptation score.
paragraphs.zh: MALO标记自有来源主题。四条Web原创描述各比较一次，每主题A、B各两次。比较对象不同，零到四原始次数不能确定二十五主题的完整排序或经过验证的适应分。

paragraphs.en: All full guides remain available before answering and when counts tie. Public links include no answers or private situation. The game cannot decide whether you should continue, cancel or accept a real responsibility; those decisions belong to the actual circumstances.
paragraphs.zh: 作答前、次数并列时，全部完整指南都可读。公开链接没有答案或私人处境。游戏不能决定真实职责该继续、取消还是接下，应回到实际条件。

title.en: Giver: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 投入付出者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Giver concerns offering time, a useful resource or a practical contribution when you care about someone or a shared activity. It records choices among descriptions, not generosity, relationship value or a duty to give. What you can offer depends on your actual resources and circumstances.
summary.zh: “投入付出者”关注在乎别人或共同活动时，提供时间、有用资源或具体帮助。它记录描述间的选择，不衡量慷慨、关系价值，也不分配付出义务。能提供什么取决于实际资源与处境。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Giver | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 投入付出者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Giver theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“投入付出者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Offering a specific contribution
title.zh: 提供一项具体投入

paragraphs.en: Giver concerns offering time, a useful resource or a practical contribution when you care about someone or a shared activity. It records choices among descriptions, not generosity, relationship value or a duty to give. What you can offer depends on your actual resources and circumstances.
paragraphs.zh: “投入付出者”关注在乎别人或共同活动时，提供时间、有用资源或具体帮助。它记录描述间的选择，不衡量慷慨、关系价值，也不分配付出义务。能提供什么取决于实际资源与处境。

paragraphs.en: You can recognize these descriptions and still decline a request. You can care deeply without having spare time or money. Conversely, contributing more does not establish that a relationship is mutual, safe or likely to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 认得这些描述，仍可以拒绝请求；没有多余时间或钱，也可以十分在乎。反过来，多投入也不能证明关系互惠、安全或会持续。

title.en: One useful hour rather than an open commitment
title.zh: 有用的一小时，而非无限承诺

paragraphs.en: A friend is moving and asks whether you can help. You offer one hour to label boxes because that fits your availability. The contribution is specific and freely chosen; it does not silently include transport, payment or staying until everything is finished.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友搬家问能否帮忙，你按自己的时间，提出用一小时标记箱子。投入具体且出于自愿，不默默包含交通、付款或必须留到全部结束。

paragraphs.en: The friend may prefer another kind of help or may decline. That response does not make your offer worthless. Asking what would actually help, and accepting the answer, is different from deciding for another person what they should need.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友可能更需要别的帮助，也可能婉拒，这不使提议失去价值。先问什么真正有用并接受回答，不同于替别人决定应该需要什么。

title.en: Contribution and consent belong together
title.zh: 投入也需要双方同意

paragraphs.en: An appropriate contribution can support a shared activity, but its usefulness is an outcome to discuss. The theme cannot prove effectiveness or affection. An unsolicited offer is still an offer, and the recipient may not want it or owe a particular emotional response.
paragraphs.zh: 合适投入可能支持共同活动，但是否有用需要讨论实际结果。主题不能证明效果或感情。主动帮助仍是提议，对方可以不想要，也不欠规定的情绪回应。

paragraphs.en: Offering extra before checking capacity can make it difficult to change your mind later. If you notice resentment, exhaustion or a hidden expectation of return, examine the actual agreement. Giving does not require ignoring those signals or continuing an unwanted arrangement.
paragraphs.zh: 没核对余地就多承担，之后可能不好改口。发现怨气、疲惫或未说出的回报期待时，可以检查实际约定。付出不要求忽略这些信号，也不要求继续不想要的安排。

title.en: Care, appreciation and resources
title.zh: 照应、感谢与资源

paragraphs.en: Caregiver concerns noticing comfort or offering personal care. Giver emphasizes a practical contribution. The actions can overlap, but spending time on a task does not necessarily provide the kind of comfort another person wants.
paragraphs.zh: “照应者”关注舒服程度与个人关心；本主题强调具体投入。行动可以重叠，但花时间做事，不一定提供了别人想要的安慰。

paragraphs.en: Resource Keeper checks ongoing demands before agreeing. Appreciator acknowledges something received. You can combine a careful limit, a contribution and a thank-you in one interaction. Their separate counts cannot create a kindness balance or an account of who owes whom.
paragraphs.zh: “资源守护者”答应前核对后续要求，“记好者”感谢收到的帮助。一次互动可以同时有谨慎限度、投入与感谢；次数不能组成善良平衡或谁欠谁的账。

title.en: Make the offer and its limit explicit
title.zh: 把提议与限度一起说出

paragraphs.en: If useful, ask what would help before volunteering. State one contribution you freely want and can afford to make: “I can review this section tonight, but I cannot take the whole project.” Leave space for the other person to decline or suggest something else.
paragraphs.zh: 如果合适，可以先问需要什么，再主动承担。说出一项自愿且负担得起的投入：“今晚能帮看这一节，但不能接整个项目。”给对方拒绝或另提建议的空间。

paragraphs.en: After the task, consider whether the agreement remained clear and whether you want to repeat it. No exercise is necessary. You do not have to contact anyone, spend money or prove that your result deserves the word “giver.”
paragraphs.zh: 完成后，看约定是否一直清楚，以及是否还愿意再做。练习可不做，无需联系谁、花钱或证明自己配得上“付出者”名称。

title.en: A theme about chosen effort, not obligation
title.zh: 自愿投入的主题，不是义务

paragraphs.en: ATM is retained only as the owned source identifier. The Web repair uses four new descriptions of affordable, voluntary contributions, not a financial or relationship role. Their counts come from four scheduled opponents, with equal A/B positions, and establish no norm or full ordering of twenty-five themes.
paragraphs.zh: ATM仅保留为自有来源标识。Web修订新写四条可负担、自愿投入的描述，不安排财务或关系角色。次数来自四个固定比较对象，A/B位置均等，不建立常模或二十五主题完整排序。

paragraphs.en: Every full guide is free without answering; public explanation links contain no private resources, responses or counts. Your right to refuse does not depend on a result. Real financial, care or employment obligations require their own facts and agreements.
paragraphs.zh: 不作答也能免费读全部指南，公开解释链接没有私人资源、回答或次数。拒绝权不取决于结果；真实财务、照护或劳动义务，需要各自事实与约定。

title.en: Reflective Thinker: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 反复思考者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Reflective Thinker concerns considering another explanation, clarifying a problem, following how its parts connect and revising an interpretation when information changes. These are self-descriptions, not a test of reasoning accuracy, intelligence, insight or educational level.
summary.zh: “反复思考者”关注考虑其他解释、厘清问题、追踪各部分联系，以及信息变化后修正理解。这是自述，不测试推理准确度、智力、洞察或教育水平。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Reflective Thinker | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 反复思考者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Reflective Thinker theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“反复思考者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Clarifying before settling on an explanation
title.zh: 先厘清，再确定一种解释

paragraphs.en: Reflective Thinker concerns considering another explanation, clarifying a problem, following how its parts connect and revising an interpretation when information changes. These are self-descriptions, not a test of reasoning accuracy, intelligence, insight or educational level.
paragraphs.zh: “反复思考者”关注考虑其他解释、厘清问题、追踪各部分联系，以及信息变化后修正理解。这是自述，不测试推理准确度、智力、洞察或教育水平。

paragraphs.en: Taking time to think can produce a helpful interpretation, an unhelpful one or no decision yet. The count cannot distinguish them. You may prefer reflection in a personal question and a familiar routine in an ordinary task without contradicting the theme.
paragraphs.zh: 花时间想，可能得到有用解释、无用解释，也可能暂时没有决定。次数不能区分。对个人问题偏向思考、对普通任务沿用熟悉习惯，可以并存。

title.en: A short reply with several possible meanings
title.zh: 一条短回复的几种可能

paragraphs.en: Someone answers a long message with one sentence. Before deciding they are dismissing you, you consider time pressure, a different communication style or an unanswered part they missed. Those are possibilities to check, not facts the theme authorizes you to assume.
paragraphs.zh: 一条长消息只收到一句回复。先不确定对方轻视自己，而是考虑时间紧、沟通习惯不同，或漏看了部分问题。这些是待核可能，不是主题允许直接认定的事实。

paragraphs.en: If the answer matters, a clear follow-up may provide more information than another private theory. Reflection can lead to asking, acting or leaving uncertainty alone. It does not require finding a charitable explanation for repeated poor treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果答案重要，一句明确追问可能比继续私下推想更有信息。思考可以通向询问、行动或保留未知；不要求为反复不当对待寻找善意解释。

title.en: Understanding and deciding are related tasks
title.zh: 理解与决定是相关但不同的任务

paragraphs.en: Clarifying the question may prevent work on the wrong problem. Whether it does depends on what you actually discover. A detailed explanation can still be mistaken, and a quick answer can sometimes be adequate; the result does not reward complexity for its own sake.
paragraphs.zh: 厘清问题可能避免忙错方向，但是否如此取决于实际发现。详细解释也可能错，快速答案有时已足够；结果不为了复杂而奖励复杂。

paragraphs.en: Reopening every interpretation can make it hard to choose a next step. Ask whether another fact would change the decision or simply add detail. A temporary conclusion can include what remains unknown and when you would reconsider it.
paragraphs.zh: 不断重开每种理解，也可能使下一步难以确定。可以问再多一个事实会改变决定，还是只增加细节。暂时结论可以同时写明未知，以及何时重看。

title.en: Reflection is not self-criticism or warning
title.zh: 思考不等于苛责或预警

paragraphs.en: Self-Critic concerns a harsh review of your own performance. Reflective Thinker concerns explanations and connections, which need not blame anyone. Repeated thought can contain either theme, both or neither; frequency alone does not establish a disorder or a useful habit.
paragraphs.zh: “自我苛责者”关注严厉评价自己的表现；本主题关注解释与联系，不必责怪任何人。反复想可以涉及任一主题、两者或都不是；频率本身不能确定障碍或有用习惯。

paragraphs.en: Risk Watcher emphasizes a possible obstacle or uncertain dependency. Reflection can also concern an interesting idea with no warning involved. Their raw counts cannot determine who thinks more deeply or makes better decisions.
paragraphs.zh: “预警者”偏向可能障碍与不确定条件；思考也可以围绕毫无警示意义的有趣想法。原始次数不能确定谁想得更深、决定更好。

title.en: Distinguish observation, interpretation and next step
title.zh: 区分观察、解释与下一步

paragraphs.en: For a small question, write three short lines: what you observed, one possible interpretation and one way to learn more. Mark the interpretation as provisional. You may choose no action if the issue does not matter enough to pursue.
paragraphs.zh: 面对小问题，写三行：看见什么、一种可能解释，以及一个获取信息的办法。把解释标作暂定。问题不值得继续时，也可以不采取行动。

paragraphs.en: Set a stopping point that fits the stakes, then review whether the exercise clarified anything. There is no requirement to keep analyzing. The guide does not diagnose overthinking or provide treatment for persistent distress.
paragraphs.zh: 按事情重要程度设停止点，再看是否厘清了什么。无需一直分析。本指南不诊断想太多，也不治疗持续困扰。

title.en: A thought theme, not a cognitive score
title.zh: 思考主题，不是认知成绩

paragraphs.en: THIN-K identifies the owned source theme, not a degree of intelligence. Four original descriptions are each offered once in fixed comparisons. Equal four-time exposure and two A/two B positions do not validate a trait scale or make counts a complete ranking across all themes.
paragraphs.zh: THIN-K标记自有来源主题，不表示智力等级。四条原创描述各在固定比较中出现一次。每主题四次、A/B各两次，不足以验证特质量表，也不使次数成为所有主题的完整排名。

paragraphs.en: All highest ties remain visible and every guide is free before answering. Public links carry no personal thoughts or answers. For consequential questions, use relevant evidence and expertise rather than treating this playful result as proof of sound judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 全部最高并列保留，作答前可免费读每份指南。公开链接没有私人想法或回答。重大问题需要相关证据与专业知识，不把趣味结果当判断可靠的证明。

title.en: Independent Walker: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 独行者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Independent Walker concerns first trying part of an ordinary problem alone, taking private time before talking, enjoying a solo activity and naming the support you want. It does not measure loneliness, attachment, self-sufficiency or whether you have people available to help.
summary.zh: “独行者”关注普通问题先独自处理一部分、交谈前私下整理、享受个人活动，以及说清想要的支持。不测孤独、依恋、自足能力，也不判断是否有人能帮忙。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

title.en: Independent Walker | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 独行者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南

description.en: Read the complete Independent Walker theme: concrete examples, tradeoffs, neighboring themes and an optional reflection. Free; no personality diagnosis.
description.zh: 免费完整阅读“独行者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Keeping some parts in your own hands
title.zh: 把一部分先留在自己手里

paragraphs.en: Independent Walker concerns first trying part of an ordinary problem alone, taking private time before talking, enjoying a solo activity and naming the support you want. It does not measure loneliness, attachment, self-sufficiency or whether you have people available to help.
paragraphs.zh: “独行者”关注普通问题先独自处理一部分、交谈前私下整理、享受个人活动，以及说清想要的支持。不测孤独、依恋、自足能力，也不判断是否有人能帮忙。

paragraphs.en: A chosen solo activity is different from unwanted isolation. Likewise, asking for a defined part of help does not make you less independent. The four comparisons cannot reveal your family history, relationship quality or reasons for preferring privacy.
paragraphs.zh: 自愿独处活动与不想要的隔离不同；请求别人帮明确一块，也不减少独立。四次比较不能揭示家庭经历、关系质量或重视隐私的原因。

title.en: Prepare a question before asking for help
title.zh: 求助之前先整理一个问题

paragraphs.en: You try setting up an ordinary device, identify the step you cannot complete and then ask a friend about that step. You want help with the obstacle while keeping the rest in your hands. This is one possible support arrangement, not a rule for how every problem should be handled.
paragraphs.zh: 设置普通设备时，你先试一试，找到卡住的一步，再向朋友问这一步。想获得障碍处的帮助，同时自己保留其余部分。这是一种支持安排，不是每个问题都应如此处理的规定。

paragraphs.en: In a different situation, asking immediately may be the better option, especially when a mistake could cause harm. The theme gives no credit for struggling alone or delaying appropriate assistance. Your actual needs and competence matter more than a label.
paragraphs.zh: 另一情境可能适合立刻求助，尤其错误可能造成伤害时。主题不会为独自硬撑或推迟合适帮助加分；真实需要与能力范围比标签重要。

title.en: Privacy can coexist with connection
title.zh: 隐私可以与连接并存

paragraphs.en: Private preparation may help you find words for a difficult conversation. Whether it helps depends on what follows. The count cannot show emotional skill or prove that alone time is restorative. You can decide how much to share and with whom.
paragraphs.zh: 私下准备可能帮助找到谈困难事情的词，但是否有帮助取决于之后发生什么。次数不能证明情绪技巧或独处一定恢复精力。分享多少、向谁分享，可以自己决定。

paragraphs.en: If others cannot tell whether you want company or space, a brief explanation may prevent guessing. You might say that you want time alone now and would welcome a check-in later. You also do not owe anyone a full private account to justify a boundary.
paragraphs.zh: 别人看不出你想要陪伴还是空间时，简短说明可能减少猜测。例如现在想独处，晚些时候欢迎问候。但也不欠任何人一份完整私事说明来证明边界合理。

title.en: Working alone, stepping back and choosing quiet
title.zh: 独自处理、退一步与选择安静

paragraphs.en: Detached Observer concerns distance from an interaction before deciding whether to engage. Independent Walker concerns which parts to handle privately or alone. You can want a busy group activity while preferring to organize your own contribution first.
paragraphs.zh: “抽离观察者”关注参与前与互动拉开距离；本主题关注哪些部分先私下或独自处理。可以想参加热闹集体活动，同时先自行整理自己的投入。

paragraphs.en: Quiet Observer concerns leaving some achievement or status comparisons aside. A solo activity may instead be competitive or ambitious. These counts cannot decide whether you are introverted, avoidant, isolated or unusually capable.
paragraphs.zh: “静观者”关注放下一些成就或地位比较；个人活动也可能竞争性强、目标很大。次数不能确定内向、回避、孤立或能力出众。

title.en: Describe the support arrangement you want
title.zh: 说清想要怎样的支持安排

paragraphs.en: If useful, choose one manageable task and divide it into a part you want to keep and a part where help would be welcome. Ask clearly, while allowing the other person to decline. You may also choose to do the whole task together.
paragraphs.zh: 如果合适，选一项可承担任务，分出想自己保留的部分，以及欢迎帮助的部分。明确询问，同时允许对方拒绝；也可以选择全程一起做。

paragraphs.en: Later, ask whether the arrangement felt useful rather than whether you acted independently enough. A game is not a standard you must meet. You can seek connection, change the request or stop without explaining a result.
paragraphs.zh: 之后问安排是否有用，不问自己是否表现得够独立。游戏不是必须达到的标准，可以寻求连接、改变请求或停止，无需解释结果。

title.en: No biography inferred from SOLO
title.zh: 不从SOLO推断个人经历

paragraphs.en: The owned source code SOLO identifies editorial lineage only. This Web repair does not adopt a family-history or deprivation inference. Four new descriptions produce a raw count out of four scheduled comparisons, not a validated independence scale, norm or complete theme ranking.
paragraphs.zh: 自有来源代码SOLO只标记编辑脉络。Web修订不采纳家庭经历或匮乏推断。四条新描述在四个固定比较中形成原始次数，不是经过验证的独立量表、常模或完整主题排名。

paragraphs.en: All full guides are free without answering. Public links include general explanations, never your relationships or counts. Support is available to seek at any result; this game cannot decide whether a personal situation is safe or what help you should receive.
paragraphs.zh: 全部完整指南无需作答即可免费读。公开链接只有通用解释，没有个人关系或次数。无论结果都可以求助；游戏不能判断处境是否安全或应获得哪种帮助。

title.zh: 情感投入者：SBTI完整主题读法

It describes interest and investment, not desirability, attachment style, compatibility or the strength of another person’s feelings.

title.en: Making room for a chosen connection
title.zh: 为自愿选择的连接留位置

paragraphs.en: Romantic Connector concerns imagining shared experiences, giving attention to warm exchanges, expressing welcome affection and making room for a relationship you choose. It describes interest and investment, not desirability, attachment style, compatibility or the strength of another person’s feelings.
paragraphs.zh: “情感投入者”关注想象共同经历、注意温暖互动、表达双方欢迎的心意，以及为自愿选择的关系留位置。它描述兴趣与投入，不评吸引力、依恋、匹配或对方感情强度。

paragraphs.en: You can recognize the theme while single, while choosing not to date or while keeping a relationship private. A lower count does not establish coldness or an inability to love. No relationship status or intimate history is needed to read the guide.
paragraphs.zh: 单身、选择不约会或想保护关系隐私时，也可以认得主题。次数较少不表示冷漠或没有爱人的能力；阅读不需要提供关系状态或亲密经历。

title.en: An invitation rather than an assumed future
title.zh: 提出邀请，不预定两个人的未来

paragraphs.en: After a welcome conversation, you imagine visiting a small exhibition together. You make a specific invitation and leave the answer open. Your enjoyment of the possibility is yours; the other person’s interest needs their own words and choices.
paragraphs.zh: 一段双方欢迎的交谈后，你想到一起看小展览，便提出具体邀请，并让答案保持开放。期待的乐趣属于自己，对方是否有兴趣，需要对方自己的话与选择。

paragraphs.en: A kind reply is not automatically a promise of romance or a future commitment. If the other person declines, your imagined experience does not create an obligation. The theme cannot interpret mixed messages, infer consent or tell you to pursue someone.
paragraphs.zh: 友好回复不自动成为恋爱或未来承诺。对方拒绝时，自己的想象不产生对方义务。主题不能解释含混信号、推断同意或要求追求某个人。

title.en: Investment still needs room for the rest of life
title.zh: 投入也给其他生活留空间

paragraphs.en: Making time for a mutually chosen relationship can reflect something important to you. The count cannot tell whether the balance is satisfying or whether your attention is returned. Actual conversations and repeated behavior are more relevant than a playful label.
paragraphs.zh: 为双方选择的关系腾时间，可以反映重视的东西。次数不能说明平衡是否满意、关注是否得到回应。真实交谈与重复行为，比趣味标签更相关。

paragraphs.en: If the imagined future fills every gap, you might overlook practical needs or current differences. You can enjoy affection while keeping friendships, rest and personal plans. Adjusting your investment does not prove that a feeling was false or that the relationship must end.
paragraphs.zh: 如果想象的未来填满每个空隙，可能忽略实际需要或当下差异。享受心意，也可以保留朋友、休息与个人安排。调整投入不证明感情虚假，也不决定必须分开。

title.en: Affection is not the same as giving or expression
title.zh: 心意不等于付出或造型表达

paragraphs.en: Giver emphasizes contributing time or practical resources. Romantic Connector emphasizes attention to a chosen affectionate connection. A contribution can be friendly, professional or familial without romance, and affection can be meaningful without a material contribution.
paragraphs.zh: “投入付出者”强调时间或实际资源；本主题强调对自愿情感连接的关注。投入可以是朋友、工作或家人之间的，完全不涉及恋爱；心意也可以不靠物质贡献成立。

paragraphs.en: Expressive Styler concerns shaping voice or presentation, which may be entirely private or unrelated to a relationship. Neither theme establishes attractiveness. Keep their raw counts separate rather than constructing a love, popularity or partner-quality score.
paragraphs.zh: “表达造型者”关注语气或呈现，可能完全私下进行、与关系无关；两者都不确定吸引力。次数分别保留，不合成爱情、受欢迎或伴侣质量分。

title.en: Keep a wish distinct from an agreement
title.zh: 把愿望与约定分开

paragraphs.en: If useful and safe, name one experience you would enjoy sharing, then ask whether the other person would also like it. Accept their answer without using your result as persuasion. You can also reflect privately and make no invitation.
paragraphs.zh: 如果合适且安全，可以说出一项想分享的经历，再问对方是否也愿意。接受答案，不用结果说服。也可以只私下想一想，不发出邀请。

paragraphs.en: Separately note what has actually been agreed and what remains your hope. Both can matter without being confused. You do not need to start, continue or end a relationship to complete this reading; real choices require your own circumstances and boundaries.
paragraphs.zh: 另外记录实际约定了什么、什么仍只是希望。两者都可以重要，而无需混淆。不必开始、继续或结束关系来完成阅读；真实选择需要结合处境与边界。

title.en: No relationship forecast from LOVE-R
title.zh: 不从LOVE-R预测关系

paragraphs.en: LOVE-R is the owned editorial source theme. The Web repair uses four new non-intimate descriptions and counts how often you selected them in their fixed pairings. Four equal appearances per theme do not validate a love scale or provide a full comparison of all twenty-five themes.
paragraphs.zh: LOVE-R是自有编辑来源主题。Web修订新写四条不索取亲密细节的描述，只记固定配对中选了几次。每主题出现四次，不足以验证爱情量表，也不提供二十五主题的完整比较。

paragraphs.en: Every full guide is free before answering, with all highest ties retained in the personal readout. Public links contain no partner information, answers or counts. This entertainment game cannot predict a breakup, establish consent or evaluate another person.
paragraphs.zh: 作答前可免费读全部指南，个人读数保留所有最高并列。公开链接没有伴侣信息、答案或次数。娱乐游戏不能预测分手、确定同意或评价另一个人。

title.en: Surprised Commentator: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 鲜活反应者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.en: Surprised Commentator concerns quickly expressing surprise, retelling an unusual moment and asking an animated question before a full opinion forms. The descriptions concern expression, not emotional intensity, impulsivity, honesty or the accuracy of the first reaction.
summary.zh: “鲜活反应者”关注较快表达惊讶、转述不寻常场面，以及完整看法形成前先带着反应提问。描述关注表达，不测情绪强度、冲动、诚实或第一反应的准确度。

scoreReading.en: A raw count of choices: 0–4 across this theme’s four scheduled comparisons. It is not a measured trait, percentile or complete ranking of all themes.
scoreReading.zh: 原始选择次数：本主题四次固定比较中选了0—4次。不是测得的特质、百分位或所有主题的完整排名。

description.zh: 免费完整阅读“鲜活反应者”：具体场景、取舍、相近主题区别与可选观察。费马50组趣味修订版，不作人格或健康诊断。

title.en: Letting a first reaction become visible
title.zh: 让第一下反应显出来

paragraphs.en: Surprised Commentator concerns quickly expressing surprise, retelling an unusual moment and asking an animated question before a full opinion forms. The descriptions concern expression, not emotional intensity, impulsivity, honesty or the accuracy of the first reaction.
paragraphs.zh: “鲜活反应者”关注较快表达惊讶、转述不寻常场面，以及完整看法形成前先带着反应提问。描述关注表达，不测情绪强度、冲动、诚实或第一反应的准确度。

paragraphs.en: You might react visibly with close friends and remain reserved in a formal setting. Some strong feelings also stay quiet. A lower count cannot show that a person is unfeeling, and a higher count cannot reveal everything they are experiencing.
paragraphs.zh: 你可能在熟人面前明显表现，在正式场合保持克制；强烈感受也可能很安静。次数较少不表示没有感受，次数较多也不能揭示全部体验。

title.en: A changed plan prompts a question
title.zh: 计划突然变化时先问一句

paragraphs.en: You arrive expecting a small gathering and discover a much larger event. “Oh, has the plan changed?” comes out before you know how you feel about it. The question can open a conversation; it is not yet a final complaint, endorsement or decision to stay.
paragraphs.zh: 原以为是小聚会，到场发现活动大得多，还没确定自己的感受，就先问“咦，计划变了吗？”这可以打开交谈，但不是最终抱怨、赞同或决定留下。

paragraphs.en: After hearing the explanation, you may be pleased, uncomfortable or undecided. You can correct an early impression. Other people also need not interpret an animated reaction as permission to continue an arrangement or as a complete account of your opinion.
paragraphs.zh: 听完解释后，可能高兴、不舒服或仍没想好，都可以修正最初印象。别人也不必把生动反应理解为继续安排的许可，或对完整看法的交代。

title.en: A first response can leave room for revision
title.zh: 第一反应也可以保留修改空间

paragraphs.en: An immediate response may make your interest visible or help another person notice a change. That outcome depends on context and reception. The count does not measure communication skill, and a reaction need not be entertaining to be valid.
paragraphs.zh: 即时回应可能让兴趣可见，或提醒别人注意变化，但效果取决于情境与接收方式。次数不测沟通技能；反应不必好玩才有效。

paragraphs.en: A vivid retelling can travel further than you intend or include someone else’s private details. Before sharing, consider whose story it is and what has been checked. You can keep the expressive detail while saying, “That was my first impression; I do not know the full context.”
paragraphs.zh: 生动转述可能传得比预想更远，或包含他人隐私。分享前可以看是谁的经历、哪些已核实。保留表达也可以补一句：“这只是我第一印象，完整情况还不知道。”

title.en: Reaction, humor and pressure
title.zh: 反应、幽默与压力

paragraphs.en: Lightener emphasizes looking for a playful element; Surprised Commentator emphasizes an event prompting expression. Surprise need not be funny. You can quietly seek humor or react strongly to an unexpected detail without making a joke.
paragraphs.zh: “轻松找乐者”偏向寻找好玩之处；本主题偏向事件触发表达。惊讶不一定好笑，可以安静找乐，也可以对意外细节反应鲜明却不讲笑话。

paragraphs.en: Pressure Speaker concerns naming strain and limits. A surprised question can be neutral, delighted or concerned without expressing a boundary. The themes can overlap in an event, but their counts cannot determine emotional regulation or a permanent temperament.
paragraphs.zh: “直抒压力者”关注说压力与限度。惊讶提问可以中性、开心或关切，不一定表达边界。几个主题可在同一事件重叠，但次数不能确定情绪调节或永久气质。

title.en: Add one sentence of context
title.zh: 给反应补一句背景

paragraphs.en: For one harmless unexpected moment, notice the first thing you say and what you know afterward. If useful, add a sentence distinguishing the immediate reaction from your considered view. You need not become quieter or perform enthusiasm for anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 遇到一件无害意外小事，留意第一句话，以及之后知道了什么。需要时，补一句区分即时反应与想过的看法。无需变安静，也无需向任何人表演热情。

paragraphs.en: If you retell it, leave out identifying or private details that are not yours to share. You can also keep the moment to yourself. This is an optional observation, not a practice for making a personality label more convincing.
paragraphs.zh: 如果转述，略去不该由自己分享的身份或私人细节；也可以只留给自己。这是可选观察，不是为了表现得更像人格标签。

title.en: WOC is a source identifier, not a judgment
title.zh: WOC是来源标识，不作评价

paragraphs.en: This repaired theme uses four original descriptions without requiring profanity or a particular dramatic style. Each is offered once, with two A and two B positions for the theme. The raw count has no norm, clinical threshold or complete twenty-five-theme ranking.
paragraphs.zh: 修订主题采用四条原创描述，不要求粗口或戏剧化表现。每条出现一次，主题整体A、B各两次。原始次数没有常模、临床阈值或二十五主题完整排名。

paragraphs.en: Every full guide is free without answering. Public explanations contain no personal reaction, response or count. All highest ties are allowed; the result cannot tell how you should speak in a real workplace, relationship or emergency.
paragraphs.zh: 全部完整指南无需作答即可免费读。公开解释没有个人反应、答案或次数。全部最高并列都允许；结果不能规定真实工作、关系或紧急情境该怎样说话。

title.en: Atmosphere Seeker: Full SBTI Theme Guide
title.zh: 氛围体验者：SBTI完整主题读法

summary.zh: “氛围体验者”关注为了气氛与享受选择音乐、散步、晚间小仪式或轻松聚会。不测心情、外向、逃避或物质使用。四条描述不询问饮酒，也不暗示需要酒精。

title.en: Atmosphere Seeker | SBTI 50-Choice Theme Guide
title.zh: 氛围体验者｜SBTI费马50组修订版指南
